blurb: Orientation: what APEX is, the pipeline, the command surface, the repo layout.
html:
APEX - AI Product Execution Framework

Status: IN IMPLEMENTATION Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-04-23

Git-based product development process with AI augmentation. APEX transforms how Product Managers create, validate, and deliver product specifications.

What is APEX?

APEX (AI Product Execution) is a hypothesis-driven product development framework that:

  • Uses Git repositories as the single source of truth for all product artifacts
  • Provides AI-assisted workflows through Cursor IDE slash commands (29 skills)
  • Automates PRD generation from initiative context (meetings, discovery, experiments)
  • Enables JIRA Epic/Story generation from approved PRDs
  • Tracks initiative → experiment → PRD → code → ship → learn pipeline

Pipeline Overview

INITIATIVE → EXPERIMENTS → PRD → JIRA EPIC → CODE → SHIP → MEASURE
   (6 wks)     (2 wks ea)    (auto)   (TxDD)     (SDD)         (learn)

Quick Start

Prerequisites

# Install the apex CLI (required once)
pip install -e packages/apex-tools/

For Product Managers

  1. Open this repository in Cursor
  2. Type /apex-help to see available commands
  3. Type /apex-initiative to create a new initiative

For Engineers / Contributors

# Validate all artifacts before committing
apex validate --root .

# Check for broken links
apex check-links --root .

# Preview initiatives needing directory migration (dry-run)
apex migrate --root .

# Install git hooks
bash scripts/hooks/install-hooks.sh

# Run pre-commit hooks manually
pre-commit run --all-files

# Start Docusaurus docs site locally
cd website && npm install && npm start

Available Commands (Cursor slash commands)

Command Purpose
/apex-help Show all commands
/apex-setup First-time git identity setup
/apex-proposal Create or update a proposal
/apex-vote Upvote or downvote a product proposal
/apex-initiative Create new initiative
/apex-experiment Create experiment for initiative
/apex-prd Generate PRD from initiative context
/apex-prd-review Score PRD implementability (5-dimension quality gate)
/apex-tests Generate test manifest from approved PRD
/apex-implementation Create engineering execution plan
/apex-epic Convert approved PRD to JIRA epic
/apex-ship Record deployment milestone
/apex-measure Record metrics checkpoint
/apex-learn Document learnings and retrospective
/apex-status Show pipeline status for an initiative
/apex-dashboard Show cross-product pipeline overview
/apex-report Generate comprehensive status report
/apex-transition Transition document status
/apex-update-initiative Re-synthesize Initiative.md from subdirectory context
/apex-validate Validate frontmatter and links
/apex-commit Commit with conventional format
/apex-pr-create Create pull request with APEX conventions
/apex-pr-review Review PR with structured checklist
/apex-pr-approve Approve a pull request
/apex-pr-request-changes Request changes with structured feedback
/apex-pr-comment Add comment to a pull request
/apex-pr-report Personalized PR review report

See .cursor/skills/README.md for full skill documentation.

Repository Structure

APEX/
├── products/               # 3-level hierarchy: domain/product/initiative
│   ├── analytics/          # Data science, ML, forecasting, pricing
│   ├── applications/       # Customer-facing apps (GameChanger, Blockbuster, etc.)
│   ├── data-platform/      # Data lake, pipelines
│   ├── engineering-platform/ # Infrastructure, monolith, tooling
│   ├── integrations/       # PMS, CRS, channel connectors
│   ├── internal/           # R&D-internal tooling (includes APEX framework dogfooding)
│   └── onboarding/         # Self-service and partner onboarding
├── pods/                   # Team pod charters (TC-NNN)
├── teams/                  # Team definitions
├── policies/               # Standing operating policies (ai/, data/)
├── guides/                 # Step-by-step task guides (for-pms/, for-engineers/, for-anyone/)
├── proposals/              # Active global/cross-cutting proposals
├── templates/              # Document templates (15 templates)
├── schemas/                # JSON Schema validation (frontmatter.schema.json, repos.schema.json)
├── packages/
│   └── apex-tools/         # Installable apex CLI (validate, migrate, check-links, status-change)
│       # AI tool integration is now via the APEX Companion hosted MCP server
│       # (the APEX Companion app OAuth 2.1 PKCE — a different
│       # host than the Companion web app); packages/apex-mcp was retired per
│       # DEC-2026-018.
├── scripts/                # Automation tools and hooks
├── .cursor/
│   └── skills/             # 29 APEX Cursor IDE slash commands
├── .claude/
│   └── agents/             # 7 Claude Code agents (research, engineer, qa, ops, docs, ticketing, web-qa)
├── archive/                # Historical documents and proposals
├── examples/               # Working examples
├── newsletters/            # Product "What's New" newsletter editions
├── wiki/                   # Reference knowledge base
├── plugins/                # Plugin directory
├── docs/                   # Framework documentation
│   ├── decisions/          # Decision records (DEC-YYYY-NNN)
│   ├── plans/              # Active plans
│   ├── migration-guides/   # Migration guides
│   └── research/           # Research documents
└── website/                # DEPRECATED Docusaurus site (redirect stub → APEX Companion)

Initiative Directory Structure

Initiatives live under products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/. Each initiative is a directory containing all related artifacts:

products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/<initiative-name>/
├── Initiative.md          # Main initiative document
├── meetings/              # Meeting notes, decisions
├── discovery/             # Research, user interviews, data
├── experiments/           # Experiment docs (E-2026-XX-NNN.md)
├── designs/               # Wireframes, mockups, prototypes
├── tickets/               # JIRA ticket references
├── release-notes/         # Version history, changelogs
├── repos.yaml             # Repository linkage (optional)
└── docs/                  # Supporting documentation

Key Decisions

POD as Metadata

POD (team assignment) is stored as frontmatter metadata, not folder structure:

---
title: Example Initiative
pod: Revenue-Optimization  # Team assignment as tag
status: discovery
---

Branching Strategy

Branch prefix signals the nature of the work:

Prefix When to use
initiative/ Creating or updating an Initiative.md
proposal/ A proposal awaiting review
experiment/ An experiment artifact
prd/ A PRD artifact
guide/ A guide in guides/
policy/ A policy in policies/
decision/ A decision record (DEC-YYYY-NNN)
team/ A team charter (TC-NNN)
fix/ Status updates, minor corrections
feature/ Multi-artifact changes
docs/ Framework docs only
chore/ CI, tooling, repo maintenance

See docs/BRANCH-NAMING-CONVENTION.md for full details.

Artifact Numbering

Type Format Example
Initiative I-YYYY-XX-NNN I-2026-GC-001
Experiment E-YYYY-XX-NNN E-2026-FOR-007
PRD PRD-YYYY-XX-NNN PRD-2026-FOR-003
Implementation IMPL-YYYY-XX-NNN IMPL-2026-APX-001
Product Proposal PROP-YYYY-XX-NNN PROP-2026-GC-001
Team Charter TC-NNN TC-001
Decision DEC-YYYY-NNN DEC-2026-001

Note: Do not add an id: field to frontmatter — path-based identification is canonical.

Status Workflows

Initiative:

discovery → validated → delivery → deployed → learning → success
         ↘ killed

Experiment:

planned → running → completed
Outcome: validated | invalidated | inconclusive

PRD:

draft → review → approved → in-development → deployed → learning

Implementation:

draft → review → approved → in-progress → complete

Proposal:

draft → review → approved → implemented  (or rejected)

Product Proposal:

draft → approved → in-progress → delivered  (or rejected / duplicate / parked)

Decision:

proposed → accepted  (or deprecated / superseded)

Policy / Guide:

DRAFT → APPROVED → OBSOLETE

Validation & CI

# Validate all APEX artifacts
apex validate --root .

# Check markdown link integrity
apex check-links --root .

# Preview migrations (dry-run)
apex migrate --root .
  • Pre-commit: .pre-commit-config.yaml runs apex validate --root . on every commit
  • CI: .github/workflows/validate-apex.yml runs validation on every PR
  • Docs deploy: .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml publishes the deprecated Docusaurus site as a redirect stub (see below)

Documentation: The APEX Docusaurus site is deprecated in favor of the APEX Companion app: the APEX Companion app — website/ is now a redirect-only stub. The old domain (the APEX Companion app) redirects there pending GitHub Pages / DNS decommission.

Historical Context

The original process proposals that led to APEX are preserved in:

  • PDP Process Proposal
  • Tooling Implementation Proposal

Contributing

  1. Clone this repository
  2. Open in Cursor
  3. pip install -e packages/apex-tools/ to install the apex CLI
  4. Use /apex-setup to configure git identity
  5. Create initiatives under products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/
  6. Run apex validate --root . before committing
  7. See docs/CONTRIBUTING.md for full guidelines

Related Documentation

  • CONTRIBUTING.md - Contribution workflow and conventions
  • GOVERNANCE.md - Process change governance
  • BRANCH-NAMING-CONVENTION.md - Branch naming rules
  • Initiative: APEX Framework - This project's own initiative
  • Products Overview - All 48 initiatives across 8 domains

APEX is actively being developed using the APEX framework itself (dogfooding).

title: Guide for AI Tools
blurb: What an AI coworker reads first when it opens the APEX repository.
html:
AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coworkers

This file is the cross-tool entry point auto-read by Cursor, Claude Desktop/Cowork, and other AI coding/product agents that operate in this repository. Keep it skimmable — it points to deeper sources rather than duplicating them.

APEX (AI Product Execution) is a Git-based product development framework: every artifact (initiative, PRD, decision, guide, etc.) is a version-controlled markdown file with YAML frontmatter. For orientation, workflow, and delivery rules, start with CLAUDE.md. For the authoritative artifact model, directory structure, skills catalog, validation rules, and known discrepancies, see docs/spec/. This file does not repeat that content — it covers two specific AI-coworker workflows and restates the delivery rules that apply to everything you do here.

Documentation-Update Workflow

When a shipped/delivered initiative needs product documentation generated or updated:

  1. Trigger: the /apex-generate-docs skill (.cursor/skills/apex-generate-docs/SKILL.md). It runs against an initiative whose frontmatter has documentation_enabled: true and status shipped (external docs) or delivered (internal docs).
  2. Output: a doc artifact (DOC-YYYY-NNN.md), placed at either:
    • External: documentation-tree/{product}/DOC-YYYY-NNN.md — see documentation-tree/README.md.
    • Internal: the initiative's own products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/{slug}/documentation/internal/ — see docs/INTERNAL-DOCS-STANDARD.md for path rules and frontmatter.
  3. Voice and style: generated drafts follow the Duetto Online Help Style Guide.
  4. Review and delivery — never bot-committed: the skill writes a local draft only. A PM reviews and edits it, then commits it on a branch and opens a normal APEX PR (branch → PR → squash-merge, same as any other artifact). No automation commits doc artifacts directly.
  5. Current status: apex-generate-docs is a Phase-1 stub — full three-pillar generation (Apex context + repo docs + JIRA) lands in Phase 2 of proposals/AUTOMATED-PRODUCT-DOCS-PIPELINE.md (PROP-2026-DOC-001), alongside the APEX Companion generation backend (DEC-2026-014).

Newsletter-Update Workflow

When adding a "What's New" item for the apex-companion hub:

  1. Trigger: the /apex-newsletter skill (.cursor/skills/apex-newsletter/SKILL.md). It creates individual, dated updates only — one file per item.
  2. Output: newsletters/{domain}/updates/YYYY-MM-DD-{slug}.md, where {domain} is product or engineering. See newsletters/product/README.md (or newsletters/engineering/README.md) for the frontmatter schema.
  3. Out of scope for this skill: edition-level roll-ups under newsletters/{domain}/editions/. Editions are curated narratives assembled from multiple updates and are created exclusively by the create_newsletter_edition MCP tool plus the narrative-synthesis curation process — do not attempt to build or trigger edition creation from this skill.
  4. Delivery: same as any APEX content — publishing means merging a PR to main, gated by the CODEOWNERS entry for the relevant newsletters/{domain}/** path. Writes never commit to main directly.

Delivery Rules (non-negotiable)

These apply to every change an AI coworker makes in this repo, documentation or otherwise — see CLAUDE.md for the full detail:

  • Never commit directly to main — branch protection enforces this.
  • Branch → commit → PR → squash-merge. main requires 1 code-owner approval + passing checks (validate-frontmatter, check-pod-merge).
  • Run apex validate --root . before committing (requires pip install -e packages/apex-tools/ once). This catches frontmatter/link errors before they reach CI.

Claude Desktop / Cowork Setup

If you're setting up or using APEX from Claude Desktop (Cowork) rather than a repo checkout, connect to the APEX Companion MCP connector (hosted, OAuth 2.1 PKCE, 30+ tools) at the APEX Companion app instead of a local package install — packages/apex-mcp was retired per DEC-2026-018. Note this connector endpoint is a different host than the Companion web app (the APEX Companion app). See the APEX Companion docs for further connector setup detail.

title: Normative Specification
blurb: The spec catalog, the precedence order between layers, and the artifact model map.
html:
APEX Framework Normative Specification {#SPEC-APEXSPEC-01~draft}

Status: Normative · Subsystem: APEXSPEC · Last-updated: 2026-07-31 · Spec ID: SPEC-APEXSPEC-01~draft

What APEX Is

APEX (AI Product Execution) is a Git-based product development framework in which every product artifact — strategic bets, validated experiments, requirements, technical designs, implementation plans, and standing records — is a markdown file with validated YAML frontmatter, version-controlled in this repository. Artifacts are organized under a three-level product hierarchy (products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/{slug}/), linked to one another by explicit ID references, and advanced through well-defined status lifecycles using /apex-* skills (Cursor) and Claude Code agents. The framework is enforced by a JSON Schema (schemas/frontmatter.schema.json), the installable apex CLI (packages/apex-tools/), the APEX Companion hosted MCP server, pre-commit hooks, and CI workflows. APEX is "PM-as-code": the same review, branching, and merge discipline applied to software is applied to product decisions.

Status & Authority

This specification is normative and as-built: it documents how APEX actually works in this repository as of the updated date, not how it is aspirationally described. It is the reference contract for the artifact model, field requirements, lifecycles, validation, and tooling.

Precedence order

Where sources disagree, the following precedence resolves the conflict (highest authority first):

  1. schemas/frontmatter.schema.json — the canonical frontmatter contract. Required fields, enums, ID patterns, and conditional requireds are authoritative here.
  2. templates/ — the document templates (initiative-template.md, prd-template.md, etc.). Authoritative for document body structure and default frontmatter scaffolding.
  3. website/docs/ handbook + .cursor/skills/ — the operational handbook and the 38 Cursor skills (SKILL.md per skill). Authoritative for workflow procedure.
  4. CLAUDE.md / README.md — orientation and quick-reference. Lowest authority; subject to drift.

Discrepancies between these layers are tracked in 07-known-discrepancies.md as numbered reconciliation items (DISC-1..DISC-25). They represent gaps to be fixed; this spec records the as-built state and the recommended normative resolution for each.

Change control

Any change to artifact IDs, status enums, required fields, or cross-artifact linkage MUST be propagated through all authority layers in this order: schema → templates → skill docs → handbook → apex-tools validator. A change that lands in only one layer is a discrepancy.

Normative Coverage Map (NCM)

The change-control rule above states that layers must stay in sync but provides no way to find the layers that implement a given rule, and no way to check that the link still resolves. Prose then restates what code enforces and silently drifts — the failure mode recorded as DISC-14 through DISC-19. NCM is the convention that closes it. It is defined here, rather than in any one spec document, because it is a cross-layer mechanism that applies to every normative rule in docs/spec/; scoping it to a single document would guarantee the others never adopt it.

Naming note — NCM is not SLD. This convention was introduced on 2026-07-16 under the name "Spec Linked Docs (SLD)". That name was squatted: it was chosen after searching only this repository, and an established standard of that name already existed — Spec-Linked Documentation (DOC-38) in bobmatnyc/trusty-tools. The two mechanisms are incompatible, not variants: canonical SLD is unidirectional (source → spec, "a resolver never invents linkage"), keys on spec_refs: (plural, list of {id, path, anchor} maps), and names four-status traceability enforcement an explicit non-goal (§1.3, §6: "a resolver reads links; it does not gate on coverage"). This convention is bidirectional and its whole point is the ENFORCED/GAP coverage tag — precisely the thing canonical SLD declines to attempt. Keeping the name would have implied conformance to a standard this mechanism deliberately contradicts, so the convention was renamed to NCM and the SLD name returned to its owner. Canonical SLD is adopted separately and additively — see Spec-Linked Documentation (SLD, canonical) below. The two coexist: NCM answers "who implements this rule, and does code prove it?"; SLD answers "which spec section governs this file?". Recorded as DISC-24.

NCM is two reciprocal links and nothing else:

  1. Spec → implementers. A normative section that is realised elsewhere carries an **NCM:** line naming each implementing artifact by path, with file:line where the rule is a specific check. Each entry is tagged ENFORCED (code proves it) or GAP (nothing proves it yet). A section with no implementers carries no line.

  2. Implementer → spec. Each named artifact carries a reciprocal backlink to the section that governs it, in the cheapest carrier that file type already has:

    Implementer Carrier
    Markdown artifact (policy, guide, decision, …) ncm_ref: frontmatter key
    Markdown artifact whose schema sets additionalProperties: false (e.g. doc) an **NCM:** line in the body
    Python module a Spec: line in the module docstring
    JSON Schema a "$comment" naming the spec section

    Backlinks MUST be anchored — path#section-anchor, not a bare file path. A file-level ref names the document but not the rule, so nothing can check that the cited section still exists, which is the only half worth checking. ncm_ref: takes a single string or a list when an artifact implements several sections.

The key is ncm_ref:, deliberately not spec_ref:. The original key was one character away from canonical SLD's spec_refs: — a singular/plural distinction carrying a total difference in meaning (direction, value shape, ID grammar). That is a trap for both readers and any future parser, so the NCM key is now lexically distinct from the SLD key and the two can coexist in the same frontmatter block without ambiguity.

ncm_ref: needs no schema change: every markdown artifact type that carries it today is additionalProperties: true (schemas/frontmatter.schema.json — policy, guide, decision, initiative, implementation).

Why it is checkable. Both directions are greppable strings, which is what made the pass below buildable: every **NCM:** target must resolve to a real path whose file carries a backlink naming the citing document, and every ncm_ref: must resolve to a real file and a real section anchor.

The pass exists — ENFORCED (warning severity) since 2026-07-16. _check_ncm (packages/apex-tools/src/apex/services/validation.py:1667, called at :305) checks both edges on every apex validate run: (1) every ncm_ref: frontmatter entry on any loaded artifact must be an anchored path#section-anchor whose file exists and whose anchor matches a real heading (GitHub-slugger compatible — github_heading_slug, :69); (2) every implementer named in a **NCM:** marker block in docs/spec/*.md must exist and carry a reciprocal backlink in its type's carrier from the table above. Rows a spec honestly tags GAP are skipped — the pass verifies claims, not aspirations — and findings are WARNINGS while the convention has a single adopter, so a doc-link rot cannot block artifact CI. This closed G8 in 08-repo-linkage.md §11.

Cost control. NCM is deliberately not required everywhere. It is REQUIRED only for normative rules that code enforces or must enforce; it is OPTIONAL for narrative prose. A convention with high authoring cost gets skipped, which is the drift it exists to prevent.

Spec-Linked Documentation (SLD, canonical)

SLD is an external standard, not an APEX invention: DOC-38 — Spec-Linked Documentation in bobmatnyc/trusty-tools (Status: Draft; SPEC-SLD-01~draft…SPEC-SLD-03~draft). That document is the sole authority for anything called SLD; this section records how APEX adopts it and, honestly, how far APEX currently conforms. Where this section and DOC-38 disagree, DOC-38 wins and this section is the defect.

SLD is a linkage convention: a source artifact declares which spec section governs it, so a resolver can trace the artifact back to that section. It is declared-links-only — "a resolver never invents linkage, never infers it from names/paths, and never treats absence as an error" (§0). A file that declares nothing is a valid, unremarkable state.

The form APEX uses

APEX is a Markdown repository, so the canonical declaration form is spec_refs: YAML frontmatter (DOC-38 §2.5, §3.6), whose entries are structured maps:

---
spec_refs:
  - id: SPEC-LINKAGE-01~draft          # required; matches the SPEC-ID grammar (§2.1)
    path: docs/spec/08-repo-linkage.md # required; MUST be repo-root-relative
    anchor: SPEC-LINKAGE-01~draft      # required; MUST equal `id`
    note: optional free text           # optional; never parsed by a resolver
---
  • ID grammar (§2.1): SPEC-{SUBSYSTEM}-{NN}~{rev} — SUBSYSTEM is /[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]*/, NN is /[0-9]{2,}/ and is an opaque per-spec counter, not a section index, rev is an open lowercase token starting at draft (~draft → ~v1 → ~v2; a named tag such as ~approved is permitted — "a resolver MUST NOT reject a well-formed ~<token> revision it does not recognize").
  • Anchor equals ID (§2.1, §4.3, AC-3): a governed section anchors its ID with a {#SPEC-{SUBSYSTEM}-{NN}~{rev}} heading marker, and the reference's anchor MUST equal its id. "A section without an anchor cannot be an SLD target."
  • Path form (§2.1, §2.5): path is repo-root-relative — never file-relative. A file-relative URL is permitted only in an optional, informative visible section.
  • Catalog row (§4.5): "Every spec MUST have a row in its repository's spec catalog." A spec file without a catalog row is uncataloged — "a defect to be fixed, not a valid state."

Where APEX's catalog and namespace live — LOCAL

DOC-38 settles this and it needs no cross-repo coordination. §4.5 requires a row in "its repository's spec catalog"; §4.1 assigns numbers scan-before-claim "within its repository's spec namespace" and warns "do not conflate namespaces" where a repository maintains more than one. §6 makes it explicit as a non-goal: "Mandating any specific repository layout, spec-catalog location, or programming language — the standard is portable; §9 documents one adopter's (trusty-tools') instantiation." trusty-tools' docs/specs/README.md catalog is therefore trusty-tools' own, not a global registry.

Consequence: APEX maintains its own catalog and its own DOC-N/SUBSYSTEM namespace. APEX claims no number and files no row upstream. Token collision with a trusty-tools SUBSYSTEM is not an error across repository boundaries, but APEX SHOULD avoid the tokens trusty-tools has claimed (SLD, CONFORMANCE, CFGDIR, TMMGR, PM, HARNESS, PROVISION, …) so a token reads unambiguously when quoted cross-repo — notably PM, which is taken upstream and would be actively misleading in a product-management framework.

Conformance — what APEX honors today

DOC-38's acceptance criteria split into adopter-side (AC-1..AC-3, which APEX controls) and resolver-side (AC-4..AC-7, which describe a tool no repository has built — DOC-38 §1.3 makes resolver implementation a non-goal and defers it to follow-up F1).

AC Requirement APEX status
AC-1 Doc number assigned scan-before-claim; catalog row added (§4.1, §4.5) MET (2026-07-17) — the 9 docs/spec/*.md files are numbered DOC-1..DOC-9 and the Index table below is the conforming catalog (DOC-N/Spec ID/Subsystem columns). Closes G14.
AC-2 Visible bold-field header block: Status/Subsystem/Owner/Last-updated/Spec ID (§4.2) MET (2026-07-17) — every docs/spec/*.md file carries a **Status:** · **Subsystem:** · **Owner:** · **Last-updated:** · **Spec ID:** line directly under its H1.
AC-3 Every governed section carries a {#SPEC-…} anchor equal to its ID (§4.3) MET (2026-07-17) — every docs/spec/*.md H1 carries a {#SPEC-APEXSPEC-NN~draft} anchor equal to its catalog Spec ID. APEX now owns 9 SLD targets.
AC-4 The inline regex extracts the same triple from Markdown-link and bare form (§2.2) N/A (resolver-side) — APEX declares no inline blocks; APEX is Markdown-only, so the frontmatter form (§2.5) applies instead.
AC-5 An inline # Spec References block is recognized in each non-Markdown file type (§3) N/A (resolver-side) — and largely inapplicable: APEX's only non-Markdown sources are packages/apex-tools/ (Python) and schemas/ (JSON), both out of scope for this change.
AC-6 spec_refs: frontmatter resolves identically for map and bare-string entries (§2.5) Authoring-side: CONFORMS by construction (APEX uses the canonical map form exclusively). Resolution unverifiable — no resolver exists.
AC-7 An existing Rust //! # Spec References block resolves unchanged (G2) N/A — APEX contains no Rust.

Honest summary: APEX conforms to canonical SLD's adopter-side obligations as of 2026-07-17. AC-1..AC-3 are the adopter's obligations and all three are now met: the 9 docs/spec/*.md files carry DOC-1..DOC-9 numbering, a bold-field header block, and a {#SPEC-APEXSPEC-NN~draft} H1 anchor equal to each file's catalog Spec ID. The owner ratified a single flat SUBSYSTEM token, APEXSPEC, for all of docs/spec/ (roster §11.1, 2026-07-17) — no token collides (case-insensitively) with the reserved trusty-tools set (SLD, CONFORMANCE, CFGDIR, TMMGR, PM, HARNESS, PROVISION). AC-4, AC-5, and AC-7 remain N/A: they are resolver-side and APEX is a Markdown-only repository with no Rust. AC-6 conforms by construction — APEX uses the canonical spec_refs: map form exclusively; resolution itself remains unverifiable because no resolver exists in any repository (DOC-38 §1.3, follow-up F1). This closes G14 in 08-repo-linkage.md §11.2. A WARNING-severity _check_sld validator pass (packages/apex-tools/src/apex/services/validation.py) checks catalog completeness, Spec ID grammar and uniqueness, header/anchor consistency, and reserved- token collisions on every apex validate run, mirroring the _check_ncm precedent (single adopter, must not block artifact CI).

What is settled by this section: the name SLD refers to DOC-38 and nothing else in this repository; the key is spec_refs: (plural, maps); APEX's catalog and namespace are local; and NCM is a separate mechanism that does not implement, extend, or conflict with SLD.

Index

This table is APEX's canonical SLD spec catalog (DOC-38 §4.5) — the DOC-N, Spec ID, and Subsystem columns are the adopter-side catalog fields; see Spec-Linked Documentation (SLD, canonical) above.

File Description DOC-N Spec ID Subsystem
README.md This document — normative coverage map (NCM), canonical SLD adoption record, and the spec catalog/index. DOC-1 SPEC-APEXSPEC-01~draft APEXSPEC
01-architecture.md Core concepts, the 22 artifact types, concept relationships, DEC-2026-004 ticket scoping, the 3-level hierarchy, and the publishing precedence model. DOC-2 SPEC-APEXSPEC-02~draft APEXSPEC
02-artifacts.md The reference core: per-type purpose, ID pattern, location, status enum, required/optional/conditional fields for the 22 artifact types (16 with full per-type sections; prd-review, doc, retrospective, test-manifest, note, and discovery summarized via the schema). blurb: Core concepts, the 22 artifact types, the linkage graph, the product hierarchy.
html:
APEX Architecture {#SPEC-APEXSPEC-02~draft}

Status: Normative · Subsystem: APEXSPEC · Last-updated: 2026-07-08 · Spec ID: SPEC-APEXSPEC-02~draft

Core Concepts

APEX models product development as a graph of typed, version-controlled markdown artifacts. Each artifact carries a YAML frontmatter block validated against schemas/frontmatter.schema.json. The frontmatter type field is a discriminator (a JSON Schema const) that selects one of 22 artifact definitions. The body is free-form markdown scaffolded from a corresponding template in templates/.

Three invariants govern the model:

  1. Frontmatter is the contract. A document's machine-readable identity, status, and linkage live in frontmatter; the body is human prose. Validation operates on frontmatter.
  2. Position encodes identity. Most artifact IDs are derived from path and filename, not stored in frontmatter. Only decision and product-proposal carry an id: field.
  3. Status drives lifecycle and governance. An artifact's status value determines both the legal next states (see 04-workflow.md) and, for initiatives, merge eligibility for pod members.

The 22 Artifact Types

Type (type: value) One-line purpose
initiative A strategic bet with a hypothesis to validate; the root artifact.
experiment A time-boxed validation of a hypothesis within an initiative.
prd Product Requirements Document auto-generated from initiative context.
prd-review Scored quality review of a PRD, produced by the apex-prd-review skill and linked to a parent PRD via parent_prd.
implementation Engineering execution plan linked to an approved PRD.
design Technical architecture design proposal scoped to an initiative.
proposal Global/cross-cutting process proposal (lives in proposals/).
product-proposal Low-friction product idea backlog item within a product folder.
decision Architectural or process decision record (ADR-style).
policy Standing, binding operating decision.
guide Step-by-step task instruction for a specific audience.
team-charter Documents a pod's structure, mission, and ways of working.
pod-charter Documents a pod's structure, mission, membership, and ownership; supersedes prior charters via superseded_by (PC-NNN).
guild-charter Documents an advisory, standards-setting guild (GC-NNN) that owns no repos, initiatives, or delivery. Requires an elt_sponsor; ownership fields are structurally unrepresentable (additionalProperties: false). Supersedes prior charters via superseded_by (GC-NNN).
wiki Reference/knowledge-base article.
update Stakeholder progress update scoped to an initiative.
rfc Request for Comments document scoped to an initiative.
doc Generated product documentation artifact (DOC-YYYY-NNN) backing the docs-generation pipeline; produced by /apex-generate-docs from a shipped/delivered initiative's three-pillar context.
retrospective Post-initiative retrospective capturing outcome and learnings, produced by the apex-learn skill and linked to its initiative via initiative_id.
test-manifest Test coverage manifest mapping acceptance criteria to tests, produced by the apex-tests skill and linked to a parent PRD via parent_prd.
note A catch-all for content worth keeping and finding that doesn't fit other types. Minimal contract (type, title, created); no ID pattern; placeable anywhere. Untyped ad-hoc notes remain valid and unaffected.
discovery Research input backing an initiative — interviews, competitive scans, source inventories, survey readouts. Lives in initiatives/{name}/discovery/. Minimal contract (type, title, status, created, author); no ID pattern. A file in a discovery/ directory is validated only if it declares a type:; untyped freeform research notes there carry no contract and are never scanned.

Concept Relationships

The Initiative is the root. Other artifacts reference it (or each other) through explicit frontmatter fields:

Field On artifact Points to Semantics
depends_on initiative [I-…] Blocking prerequisites; ordered/gating.
related_initiatives initiative, product-proposal [I-…] Related work, no ordering.
source_proposal initiative PROP-… (str or null) The product proposal that became this initiative.
related_prd initiative PRD-… (str or null) The PRD generated for this initiative.
related_experiments initiative [E-…] Experiments run under this initiative.
parent_initiative experiment, prd I-… The owning initiative.
validated_experiments prd [E-…] (may be empty) Experiments whose evidence the PRD rests on.
parent_prd implementation PRD-… The approved PRD this plan implements.
epic_ids implementation […] JIRA epic linkage (delivery).
epic_id prd str or null JIRA epic linkage (single, frontmatter only).
initiative design, update, rfc I-… or dirname The owning initiative.
initiative_id retrospective I-… or dirname The owning initiative whose outcome/learnings this retrospective captures.
parent_prd test-manifest PRD-… The PRD whose acceptance criteria this manifest maps to tests. 
graph LR
    PROP[product-proposal<br/>PROP-…] -->|source_proposal| INIT
    INIT[initiative<br/>I-…]
    INIT -->|depends_on| INIT
    INIT -->|related_initiatives| INIT
    EXP[experiment<br/>E-…] -->|parent_initiative| INIT
    INIT -->|related_experiments| EXP
    PRD[prd<br/>PRD-…] -->|parent_initiative| INIT
    INIT -->|related_prd| PRD
    EXP -->|validated_experiments| PRD
    IMPL[implementation<br/>IMPL-…] -->|parent_prd| PRD
    PRD -->|epic_id| JIRA[(JIRA Epic)]
    IMPL -->|epic_ids| JIRA
    DES[design] -->|initiative| INIT
    RFC[rfc] -->|initiative| INIT
    UPD[update] -->|initiative| INIT

Ticket-Reference Scoping (DEC-2026-004)

Decision DEC-2026-004 governs where JIRA/ticket references may appear, to keep strategy-level artifacts free of implementation churn. The rules are scope-by-artifact:

Artifact Allowed ticket references Prohibited
Initiative jira_project in frontmatter only (board-level). No inline ticket IDs, no issue tables.
PRD epic_id in frontmatter only. No inline issue tables.
Implementation Everything — epics, issues, tables, sprints, inline. (none)
Experiment Inline references allowed. (none)
repos.yaml jira_link at board level only. No per-issue links.

Rationale: an Initiative is a strategic bet whose validity does not change when a sprint re-tickets; a PRD anchors to a single epic; the Implementation is the correct home for granular delivery tracking. Experiments cite specific tickets inline because their evidence is concrete.

The 3-Level Product Hierarchy

Initiatives live three levels deep:

products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/{slug}/
  • domain — one of 7 values (see 03-directory-structure.md): analytics, applications, data-platform, engineering-platform, integrations, internal, onboarding.
  • product — one of 38 product slugs (see 03-directory-structure.md).
  • initiative slug — a kebab-case directory name matching the initiative's branch slug.

Both domain and product are also frontmatter fields on initiatives and product proposals, and both are validated against the schema enums. The path and the frontmatter MUST agree (validation pass 3 enforces directory placement).

Publishing / Source-of-Truth Precedence

APEX uses a layered authority model. The canonical source for any given fact is the highest applicable layer:

  1. schemas/frontmatter.schema.json — IDs, statuses, required fields, enums, conditionals.
  2. templates/ — body structure and default scaffolding.
  3. website/docs/ handbook + .cursor/skills/ — operational procedure.
  4. CLAUDE.md / README.md — orientation.

The repository (products/ and the standalone record directories) is the single source of truth for artifact content. Within an artifact, frontmatter overrides body prose. Across layers, a lower layer never overrides a higher one; when it appears to, that is a tracked discrepancy (07-known-discrepancies.md). Change control requires that any contract change propagate through every layer in order (schema → templates → skills → handbook → validator).

title: Artifact Reference
blurb: Per-type purpose, ID pattern, location, status enum, and required fields.
html:
APEX Artifact Reference {#SPEC-APEXSPEC-03~draft}

Status: Normative · Subsystem: APEXSPEC · Last-updated: 2026-07-17 · Spec ID: SPEC-APEXSPEC-03~draft

This is the reference core of the specification. For each of 16 of the schema's 22 artifact types (prd-review, doc, retrospective, test-manifest, and note are not yet covered here, summarized via the schema) it lists the canonical contract drawn from schemas/frontmatter.schema.json. Field lists are exact.

Conventions used below:

  • Required fields cause a validation error if absent.
  • Optional fields are permitted; unknown fields are warnings (additionalProperties:true).
  • Conditional rules are allOf if/then clauses keyed on another field's value.
  • "ID in frontmatter?" states whether the artifact's ID is stored in id: (only decision and product-proposal) or derived from path/filename.
  • title length constraints are noted per type (1–140 or 1–200, etc.).

1. Initiative

  • Purpose: A strategic bet with a hypothesis to validate. The root artifact of the model.
  • ID pattern: I-YYYY-XX-NNN (e.g., I-2026-GC-001). NOT in frontmatter; derived from the directory path.
  • Location (base): products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/{slug}/Initiative.md. (status-directory-moved): products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/{status}/{slug}/Initiative.md. All initiatives — moved or not — live under the initiatives/ umbrella. Directory movement is not terminality: only success and killed are terminal; deployed and learning move directories without being finished (see 08-repo-linkage.md §8.3).
  • Status enum: discovery | validated | delivery | delivered | deployed | shipped | learning | success | killed (9 values, per schemas/frontmatter.schema.json definitions.initiative.properties.status.enum). delivered and shipped are schema-valid but currently unused in practice (0 of 167 initiatives on disk) — prefer deployed. They carry no distinct workflow-diagram state (see 04-workflow.md).
  • Required: type, title (1–140), status, domain, product, created, updated, tags (min 1).
  • Conditional required:
    • status == discovery ⇒ metric_target, hypothesis, author, pod.
    • status ∈ {delivery, deployed, learning, success} ⇒ eng_exec_sponsor.
  • Optional: feature, metric_target, hypothesis, confidence (low|medium|high), max_experiments, time_box (deprecated), asset_type_target (full-service-hotels|limited-service-hotels|resorts|casinos|internal|all), rpos_focused, rpos_details, beta_partner ({has_partner, partner_name}), contractual_commitment, contractual_commitment_customer, enhancement_request, enhancement_request_details, author, team, pod, eng_exec_sponsor, pm_exec_sponsor, related_experiments[], related_prd (str|null), source_proposal (str|null), depends_on[], related_initiatives[], version (^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$, MAJOR.MINOR), version_history[] ({version, date, change}), target_user (enum of roles: CCO, CFO, VP_DIST, VP_RM, VP_SALES, ASSET_MGR, IT_DIR, CONTROLLER, DIST_MGR, DOC, DOS, GM, PROP_RM, CLUSTER_RM, DORM, DIR_ANCILLARY, VP_CASINO), resources[] ({person, type, allocation, role?}).

2. Experiment

  • Purpose: A time-boxed validation of a hypothesis within an initiative.
  • ID pattern: E-YYYY-XX-NNN (e.g., E-2026-FOR-007). Path/filename-based, not in frontmatter.
  • Location: …/initiatives/{slug}/experiments/E-….md.
  • Status enum: planned | running | completed.
  • Required: type, title (1–140), parent_initiative, status, hypothesis ({statement, validation_method}), success_criteria, learning ({outcome}), created, updated, author, tags.
  • Optional: hypothesis.confidence, validation_method enum (interview | analytics | prototype | a_b_test | spike), time_box (deprecated, DEP-002), learning.outcome (validated | invalidated | inconclusive | null), learning.key_insight, learning.recommendation, learning.evidence[], sample_size (str|int|null), confidence_level (number|null, a proportion in [0,1]), minimum_detectable_effect (str|number|null), completed_date (date|null), actual_sample_size (str|int|null).

3. PRD

  • Purpose: Product Requirements Document auto-generated from initiative context (meetings, discovery, experiments). Triggers JIRA Epic creation downstream.
  • ID pattern: PRD-YYYY-XX-NNN (e.g., PRD-2026-FOR-003). Path-based; NOT in frontmatter.
  • Location: …/initiatives/{slug}/PRD.md or …/initiatives/{slug}/PRD-YYYY-XX-NNN.md.
  • Status enum: draft | review | approved | in-development | deployed | learning.
  • Required: type, title (1–140), status, version (semver X.Y.Z), created, updated, author, parent_initiative, validated_experiments[] (may be empty), approvers (min 1).
  • Optional: epic_id (str|null, frontmatter only — see DEC-2026-004), executive_sponsor, stakeholders[], approval_status[], tags, priority (str|null — P0–P3 or low/medium/high/critical), target_quarter (str|null — human quarter, e.g. "Q3 2026"), product_area (str|null).

4. Implementation

  • Purpose: Engineering execution plan linked to an approved PRD. Home for granular ticket tracking (DEC-2026-004).

  • ID pattern: IMPL-YYYY-XX-NNN (e.g., IMPL-2026-APX-001). Path-based.

  • Location: …/initiatives/{slug}/implementation/ or …/initiatives/{slug}/Implementation.md.

  • Status enum: draft | review | approved | in-progress | complete.

  • Required: type, title (1–140), status, version (semver), created, updated, author, parent_prd, parent_initiative.

  • Optional: epic_ids[], tags, owner, jira_project (str|null, same shape as initiative.jira_project), tickets (object of {area: [ticket-id, ...]}), section (str — which slice of a multi-part initiative this plan covers), target_quarter (str|null, same shape as prd.target_quarter), duration (str|null — free-text estimate), parent_tech_spec (str — slug/filename of a companion tech-spec, itself often type: implementation), progress (integer 0–100), version_history (array of {version, date, change}, same shape as initiative.version_history), execution (object — see below).

  • execution — where the work lives and where it is tracked (#1583). A closed, namespaced block carrying four sibling lists, every one optional:

    • repositories[] — {name, paths[]?}. name is a bare slug resolved against the duettoresearch org exactly as a repos.yaml name: is (§4.3 of docs/spec/08-repo-linkage.md); paths scopes the plan to part of a monorepo, and its absence means the whole repository — the same claim a generated apex.yaml makes with paths: [/]. This is a strict subset of a repos.yaml repositories[] entry, so a plan entry can be lifted into a sidecar entry. role is deliberately absent: it belongs to the initiative→repo edge and is already recorded once in the sidecar, and a second copy on the plan would be a second authority with no rule for which wins.
    • boards[] — {key, url?}. key is a JIRA project key in the jira_project format (DEC-2026-004 clause 2); url is the board-level link, the role jira_link plays on a sidecar (clause 4). This repo has no identity for a board distinct from a project, so one is recorded by its project key and url covers a board that is not 1:1 with one.
    • epics[], tickets[] — flat JIRA keys, deliberately NOT nested under a board. A JIRA key already carries its project prefix by construction, so nesting would store the board twice per key and admit a contradiction (epics: [HOT-420] under key: ADV) that the flat form cannot express. The validator derives the board from the prefix and checks it was declared. repositories[].paths does nest, because a subpath is not derivable from a repo name and has no other carrier. Rule: nest what is not derivable, flatten what is.

    Optional, and every finding against it is a WARNING, never an error — 110 plans predate the field, and its repo resolution reads the generated repos-all.yaml, which can lag the repo. The same WARN-first runway parent_prd and DEP-001/002/003 ride. execution.epics supersedes epic_ids, and execution.tickets supersedes the work-area-grouped tickets object; both legacy fields stay valid and populated. Enforced by ValidationService._check_implementation_execution.

  • author vs owner: author is who wrote this artifact; owner (new — closes the ownership-field gap that let inferred initiative ownership get backfilled into author on ~90 plans) is who owns the underlying initiative. The two are frequently different people and must not be conflated. owner reuses the same key/shape as the owner field on team_charter/pod_charter/guild_charter; it is optional because "owner unknown" is a legitimate state these plans exist to surface.

  • additionalProperties: now false. An audit of all 109 live implementation artifacts (later re-confirmed at 110 as main moved) found 16 carrying undeclared keys; eight recurring concepts were promoted to the optional list above and the rest were normalized away (duplicates of parent_initiative, dead self-referential paths, values already recorded in each initiative's repos.yaml/Initiative.md, or restated in the artifact's own body). The one remaining holdout — restriction-guidelines-tech-spec.md — carried initiative-shaped keys (domain, product, pod, eng_exec_sponsor, pm_exec_sponsor, tech_lead, repositories) but was confirmed as a correctly-typed implementation (tech-specs/ is the sanctioned location, docs/spec/03-directory-structure.md:66). Its keys were resolved instead of the type: domain, product, pod, eng_exec_sponsor, and pm_exec_sponsor were dropped as exact duplicates of Initiative.md; repositories was dropped after its one non-repos.yaml-covered entry (duetto-playwright-e2e) was added to the initiative's repos.yaml; tech_lead (a genuinely new, one-off fact — no schema field warranted) moved into the document body. With that file normalized, a full corpus scan found zero remaining implementation artifacts with undeclared keys, so the flag was flipped.

5. Design

  • Purpose: Technical architecture design proposal for an approved initiative.
  • ID pattern: No global ID. Path-scoped: designs/<NAME>.md.
  • Location: …/initiatives/{slug}/designs/<NAME>.md.
  • Status enum: proposed | accepted | superseded.
  • Required: type, title (1–200), status, initiative (I-… or dirname), product, author, created, updated, version (^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$).
  • Optional: reviewers[], supersedes (null), superseded_by (null), tags.

6. Proposal (global)

  • Purpose: Global / cross-cutting process proposal (schema/tooling/process changes).
  • ID pattern: No schema-enforced ID pattern.
  • Location: proposals/; on terminal status moves to archive/proposals/ (via apex archive).
  • Status enum: draft | review | approved | implemented | rejected. Terminal: implemented, rejected ⇒ archive.
  • Required: type, title (1–140), status, author, created, updated.
  • Optional: subject_type (initiative | prd | policy | guide | process | schema | tooling | other), reviewers[], related_artifacts[], loe (S | M | L | XL), target_ia (path; valid against docs/IA.md), tags, blocked_on[] ({reason, owner?, since?, expected_by?}). See Blockers note below.

7. Product Proposal

  • Purpose: Low-friction product idea backlog item within a product folder; promoted to an initiative when ready. Supports voting.
  • ID pattern: PROP-YYYY-XX-NNN, regex ^PROP-[0-9]{4}-[A-Z]{2,3}-[0-9]{3}$. REQUIRED in frontmatter (id:).
  • Location: products/{domain}/{product}/proposals/ or initiative-level proposals/.
  • Status enum: draft | approved | in-progress | delivered | rejected | duplicate | parked.
  • Required: type, title (1–140), id, status, domain (7-enum), product (slug-enum), author, source (customer | cs | sales | product | engineering | partner | other), created, updated, tags.
  • Conditional required: source == customer ⇒ customer_name.
  • Optional: source_detail, customer_name, priority (low | medium | high | critical), related_products[], related_initiatives[], target_ia, blocked_on[] ({reason, owner?, since?, expected_by?}), votes[] ({voter, sentiment: up|down, date, comment?}).
  • Blockers note (for blocked_on[]): When a proposal is accepted but hasn't started, document what's holding it. Each entry has a required reason (string describing the gate), and optional owner (team/person responsible), since (date encountered), and expected_by (date or null). No link-resolution; free text is intentional — blockers may reference pilot customers, other teams, external partners, data dependencies, etc.

8. Decision

  • Purpose: Architectural or process decision record (ADR-style). Once accepted, never edited — supersede instead.
  • ID pattern: DEC-YYYY-NNN, regex ^DEC-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{3}$. REQUIRED in frontmatter (id:).
  • Location: docs/decisions/DEC-YYYY-NNN-{slug}.md or initiative-scoped …/docs/DEC-YYYY-NNN.md.
  • Status enum: proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded.
  • Category enum (required): process | architecture | tooling | governance.
  • Required: type, id, title (1–140), status, category, created, updated, author, approvers (min 1).
  • Optional: supersedes (null), superseded_by (null), tags.

9. Policy

  • Purpose: A standing, binding operating decision (e.g., AI tool usage, data classification). Merge to main = APPROVED.
  • ID pattern: No global ID; path-based.
  • Location: policies/{domain}/ (domains include ai, data, engineering, security, product).
  • Status enum: draft | approved | obsolete | migrated (per schemas/frontmatter.schema.json definitions.policy.properties.status.enum).
  • Required: type, title (1–140), status, version (^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$), author, created, updated, effective_date, tags.
  • Optional: approvers[], superseded_by (null).
  • Note: The apex-policy skill requires ≥1 approver, but the schema marks approvers optional — see DISC-2.

10. Guide

  • Purpose: Step-by-step task instruction for a specific audience.
  • ID pattern: No global ID; path-based.
  • Location: guides/{audience}/ (for-pms, for-engineers, for-anyone).
  • Status enum: draft | approved | obsolete | migrated (per schemas/frontmatter.schema.json definitions.guide.properties.status.enum).
  • Required: type, title (1–140), status, version, author, created, updated, tags.
  • Optional: audience[], difficulty (beginner | intermediate | advanced), time_estimate, related_artifact_type (null), related_skill (null).

11. Team Charter

  • Purpose: Documents a team's structure, mission, and ways of working. Teams are functional disciplines (career home, manager, standards) — distinct from pods, which are cross-functional and product-specific (see §11a Pod Charter below).
  • ID pattern: TC-NNN, encoded in the file name teams/TC-NNN-{slug}.md.
  • Location: teams/TC-NNN-{slug}.md — a flat file, not a subdirectory (21 charters on disk as of this writing, e.g. teams/TC-006-Quality-Guild.md).
  • Status field: Required. status is in team_charter's required array (schemas/frontmatter.schema.json:826-835) with enum: ["draft", "active", "obsolete"] (:856-859). E.g. teams/TC-006-Quality-Guild.md:8 carries status: obsolete.
  • Required: type, title (1–140), team_name, mission, status, created, updated, owner.
  • Optional: owned_repos[], tags.

11a. Pod Charter

  • Purpose: Documents a cross-functional, product-specific pod's roster, mission, and ways of working. A pod assembles people from multiple functional teams to deliver a specific product (teams/README.md:9-13; the taxonomy was established in commit 4fc96800, PR #292, 2026-04-09: "Teams = functional disciplines. Pods = cross-functional, product-specific.").
  • ID pattern: PC-NNN, encoded in the file name pods/PC-NNN-{slug}.md.
  • Location: pods/PC-NNN-{slug}.md — a flat file, not a subdirectory (19 charters on disk as of this writing, e.g. pods/PC-019-DataPlatform-Charter.md).
  • Status field: Required. status is in pod_charter's required array (schemas/frontmatter.schema.json:926) with enum: ["draft", "active", "obsolete"] (:933-936) — matching team_charter. Formerly optional; the asymmetry (DISC-23) was resolved 2026-07-17 by requiring it, with zero backfill needed (all 19 pods on disk already carried status:).
  • Required: type, title (1–140), team_name, mission, status, created, updated, owner.
  • Optional: superseded_by (pattern ^PC-\d{3}$, :897-900), owned_repos[], tags, status_history[] (array of {status, date, note?}, :909-921), members[] (array of {name, role, allocation, github?, email?, note?} — role is an enum of 17 codes, allocation an integer 10–100 in multiples of 10, :922-949).

11b. Guild Charter

  • Purpose: Documents an advisory, standards-setting body that owns no repositories, no initiatives, and no delivery backlog. Guilds set direction and coordinate standards across functional disciplines or practice areas (see guilds/README.md for the full Guild model and how it differs from teams and pods). A Guild is stewarded by an ELT member (elt_sponsor).
  • ID pattern: GC-NNN, encoded in the file name guilds/GC-NNN-{slug}.md.
  • Location: guilds/GC-NNN-{slug}.md — a flat file, not a subdirectory (1 charter on disk as of this writing, e.g. guilds/GC-001-Quality-Guild.md).
  • Status field: Required. status is in guild_charter's required array (schemas/frontmatter.schema.json:884-923) with enum: ["draft", "active", "obsolete"].
  • Required: type, title (1–140), guild_name, mission, status, created, updated, owner, elt_sponsor.
  • Optional: superseded_by (pattern ^GC-\d{3}$), tags.
  • Schema enforcement note: guild_charter deliberately uses additionalProperties: false (unlike team_charter and pod_charter, which are true) to structurally preclude owned_repos and other ownership fields — making "Guilds own nothing" a schema enforcement, not a convention. elt_sponsor is a required, unstructured string matching the precedent of eng_exec_sponsor, pm_exec_sponsor, and executive_sponsor; ELT membership is not gated in the schema (no roster exists in this repo).
  • Ratification: guild_name as a distinct field, additionalProperties: false, and elt_sponsor presence-only enforcement (no ELT roster) shipped in #1416 flagged as needing owner ratification — RATIFIED 2026-07-17, roster items 13–15 in 08-repo-linkage.md §11.1.

12. Wiki

  • Purpose: Reference / knowledge-base article (native or Confluence-migrated).
  • ID pattern: No global ID; path-based.
  • Location: wiki/{domain}/.
  • Status enum: draft | approved | obsolete | migrated (per schemas/frontmatter.schema.json definitions.wiki.properties.status.enum).
  • Required: type, title (1–200), status, version, author, created, updated, tags.
  • Optional: domain[], source (native | confluence-migration), migrated_from (null), superseded_by (null).

13. Update

  • Purpose: Stakeholder progress update scoped to an initiative.
  • ID pattern: No global ID; filename-dated.
  • Location: …/initiatives/{slug}/updates/YYYY-MM-DD-{slug}.md.
  • Status enum: draft | published.
  • Required: type, title (1–200), status, initiative, date_delivered, period_start, period_end, authors (min 1), version, created, updated, tags.
  • Optional: audience[].

14. RFC

  • Purpose: Request for Comments document scoped to an initiative. Comments occur in apex-companion, not as PRs.
  • ID pattern: No global ID; path-based.
  • Location: …/initiatives/{slug}/rfcs/.
  • Status enum: draft | open | accepted | rejected | withdrawn.
  • Required: type, title (1–200), status, initiative, domain, product, created, updated, author.
  • Optional: comment_deadline, tags.

ID-in-Frontmatter Summary

Artifact ID pattern id: in frontmatter?
Initiative I-YYYY-XX-NNN No (path-based)
Experiment E-YYYY-XX-NNN No (path/filename)
PRD PRD-YYYY-XX-NNN No (path-based)
Implementation IMPL-YYYY-XX-NNN No (path-based)
Design none (path-scoped) No
Proposal none No
Product Proposal PROP-YYYY-XX-NNN Yes (required)
Decision DEC-YYYY-NNN Yes (required)
Policy none No
Guide none No
Team Charter TC-NNN (file name) No
Pod Charter PC-NNN (file name) No
Wiki none No
Update none No
RFC none No

Per DISC-1, an id: field on any type other than decision or product-proposal is treated as deprecated and warned by the validator; it MUST NOT be added.

blurb: The annotated repo tree, initiative layout, and status-based directory movement.
html:
APEX Directory Structure {#SPEC-APEXSPEC-04~draft}

Status: Normative · Subsystem: APEXSPEC · Last-updated: 2026-07-31 · Spec ID: SPEC-APEXSPEC-04~draft

Annotated Repository Tree

products/                 # 3-level hierarchy: {domain}/{product}/initiatives/{slug}/
policies/                 # Standing operating policies — policies/{domain}/
guides/                   # Step-by-step guides — guides/{audience}/
notes/                    # Catch-all notes (fallback; preferred placement is contextually alongside initiatives/products/proposals)
wiki/                     # Reference articles — wiki/{domain}/
proposals/                # Active global/cross-cutting process proposals
                          #   (also at product- and initiative-level)
archive/
  proposals/              # Terminal (implemented|rejected) process proposals
templates/                # 16 document templates (one per artifact type + meeting/status)
schemas/                  # frontmatter.schema.json (canonical), repos.schema.json
packages/
  apex-tools/             # Installable `apex` CLI (validate/migrate/status-change/...)
                          #   AI-tool MCP access is via APEX Companion's hosted MCP server
                          #   (the APEX Companion app OAuth — a different
                          #   host than the Companion web app); packages/apex-mcp was
                          #   retired per DEC-2026-018.
scripts/
  hooks/                  # pre-commit auto-version-bump, install-hooks.sh
  validate_yaml_keys.py   # CI YAML-key validation
reports/                  # Local status reports (gitignored)
docs/
  spec/                   # THIS specification
  decisions/              # Global decision records (DEC-YYYY-NNN-*.md)
  plans/  research/        # Planning + research docs
  IA.md                   # Information-architecture map (target_ia validation source)
  CONTRIBUTING.md  GOVERNANCE.md
website/                  # Docusaurus documentation site + handbook
examples/                 # Working examples
pods/                     # Product pod charters (flat files) — pods/PC-NNN-{slug}.md
teams/                    # Functional team charters (flat files) — teams/TC-NNN-{slug}.md
guilds/                   # Advisory, standards-setting bodies (flat files) — guilds/GC-NNN-{slug}.md
whats-new-hub/            # What's-new / changelog hub
plugins/                  # Plugin directory
.cursor/skills/           # 38 Cursor IDE skills (one dir w/ SKILL.md each)
.claude/agents/           # 7 Claude Code agents
.claude/skills/           # Claude Code skill deployments (mirror Cursor apex-*)
.claude-mpm/              # MPM orchestration config
.github/
  workflows/              # CI (validate-apex, stale, assign-reviewers, ...)
  scripts/                # check-pod-merge.py, etc.
pod-merge-config.yml      # PLT/SELT/pod approver config

Proposals

A proposal is an RFC — a public one-pager inviting comment before an idea is canonized. Three rules are canonical:

1. Naming — proposals/[{group}/]{slug}.md. A proposal filename is a lowercase-kebab slug derived from the title, with no ID prefix and no PROPOSAL-/PROP- prefix, and no per-proposal wrapping directory. The optional leading {group}/ segment is a grouping subdirectory (rule 3), not a wrapper. Drop boilerplate (-proposal, kickoff:) when deriving the slug. Proposals carry no id: pattern — they are path-scoped (see ID Conventions).

Instead of Use
proposals/PROPOSAL-STATUS-SUBDIRECTORIES.md proposals/status-based-subdirectory-organization.md
proposals/PROP-2026-APX-008-RFC-COMMENTS.md proposals/formal-rfc-comment-periods.md
proposals/my-idea/Proposal.md proposals/my-idea.md

2. Single-document standard. A proposal is a single Markdown document. A same-named directory (proposals/{slug}/) is permitted only for supporting assets — images, diagrams — never for additional proposal prose. Multi-document content (specs, phased execution plans, tech designs) is not proposal material; it belongs to implementation artifacts (Implementation.md / implementation/, designs/, tech-specs/) once the initiative exists.

3. Grouping subdirectories (optional, one level). A subdirectory under proposals/ MAY group several independent proposals — each still a single .md file — for organization: proposals/{group}/{slug}.md. For example, proposals/hackathon-2026/team-alpha-idea.md and proposals/hackathon-2026/team-beta-idea.md are two distinct single-file proposals collected under one group. Grouping is not fragmentation — the distinction is what a subdirectory contains:

Subdirectory shape Verdict
Its direct .md children are each a valid single-file type: proposal (e.g. proposals/hackathon-2026/*.md) Allowed — grouping
Only non-.md assets (images/diagrams) for a sibling proposal .md Allowed — assets
One proposal split across multiple prose .md files in its own folder Forbidden — fragmentation (rule 2)
A generic Proposal.md wrapper filename Forbidden — fragmentation (rule 2)
A proposal .md with a same-named sibling directory holding additional prose .md files Forbidden — fragmentation (rule 2)

Grouping is one level only — proposals/{group}/{slug}.md is valid; proposals/{a}/{b}/{slug}.md is not. Fragmentation and over-deep nesting are flagged WARN-first by apex validate (services/validation.py); grouping and assets-only subdirectories never warn.

Location & lifecycle. Active proposals live in proposals/ (global) or under a product/initiative proposals/ subdirectory. Terminal proposals (implemented/rejected) move to the adjacent archive/proposals/ (run apex archive). Product-scoped proposals that shape a product standard may live under that product's namespace (e.g. products/{domain}/{product}/).

Initiative Directory Layout

An initiative is a directory, not a single file. The canonical layout:

products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/{slug}/
  Initiative.md                 # required — the initiative artifact
  PRD.md  (or PRD-YYYY-XX-NNN.md)
  Implementation.md  (or implementation/)
  TestManifest.md                # test coverage manifest, mapped to the parent PRD
  Retrospective.md                # post-initiative outcome + learnings summary
  repos.yaml                    # repo + board-level jira_link (repos.schema.json)
  proposals/                    # initiative-level product proposals
  meetings/                     # meeting transcripts (drop directly here)
  discovery/                    # discovery notes — typed files are `discovery` artifacts (see below)
  experiments/                  # E-YYYY-XX-NNN.md files
  designs/                      # design proposals (designs/<NAME>.md)
  tickets/                      # ticket-related artifacts
  release-notes/                # release notes
  docs/                         # initiative-scoped docs (incl. scoped DEC-YYYY-NNN.md)
  rfcs/                         # RFC documents
  updates/                      # YYYY-MM-DD-{slug}.md stakeholder updates

The discovery/ Directory — Declare a Type to Opt In

discovery/ is the one support directory that holds a real artifact type mixed in with prose. A markdown file there is validated if and only if it declares a type: in its frontmatter:

File in discovery/ Treated as Validated against
Declares type: discovery A discovery artifact The discovery schema definition
Declares some other type: An artifact of that type That type's definition (including IA placement)
Declares no type: at all A freeform research note Nothing — never scanned

Most files under discovery/ are the third kind and always have been: raw interview transcripts, pasted source dumps, working notes. They have never carried a contract and this rule gives them none. Writing type: discovery is the deliberate act that promotes a note into an artifact.

Mechanically, discovery stays in NON_ARTIFACT_DIRS (adapters/filesystem.py) and is listed in TYPE_OPT_IN_DIRS, which downgrades that directory's skip from absolute to conditional; the pre-existing no-type: guard supplies the other half of the rule. The sibling entries — meetings/, assets/, docs/ — are unaffected and skip unconditionally, so a file at discovery/meetings/notes.md is still invisible.

Findings on files that predate this rule are held at WARNING on repo-wide runs (_grace_discovery_backlog in services/validation.py), following the same runway docs/decisions/ took. A PR that touches one of those files runs scoped (--filter-paths) and gets full ERRORs, so the debt is paid by whoever next edits each file and new discovery artifacts are held to the schema from day one.

Status-Based Subdirectory Movement

When an initiative reaches a status-directory-moved status, its directory moves into a status-named subdirectory inside initiatives/. All initiatives — whether moved or not — live under the initiatives/ umbrella so the validator's depth check is always satisfied. Note: directory movement is not terminality. Only success and killed are terminal (gating); deployed and learning initiatives have moved directories but are not finished — see 08-repo-linkage.md §8.3:

products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/
  {slug}/                    # status: discovery | validated | delivery  (base)
  deployed/{slug}/           # status: deployed                          (moved, not terminal)
  learning/{slug}/           # status: learning                          (moved, not terminal)
  success/{slug}/            # status: success                           (moved, terminal)
  killed/{slug}/             # status: killed                            (moved, terminal)

Full canonical paths:

Status Path
discovery, validated, delivery products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/{slug}/Initiative.md
deployed products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/deployed/{slug}/Initiative.md
learning products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/learning/{slug}/Initiative.md
success products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/success/{slug}/Initiative.md
killed products/{domain}/{product}/initiatives/killed/{slug}/Initiative.md

The apex status-change command and apex migrate perform and validate these moves. Validation pass 3 enforces that the directory bucket matches the frontmatter status.

Domain Enum (7)

The domain field and the first path segment under products/ MUST be one of:

domain
analytics
applications
data-platform
engineering-platform
integrations
internal
onboarding

Note: apex is not a domain (see DISC-4); framework work maps to internal.

Product-Slug Enum

The product field and the second path segment MUST be one of a closed enum of product slugs defined in schemas/frontmatter.schema.json (definitions.product_slug.enum). A product value outside that enum fails validation, and so does a path whose second segment does not match the artifact’s declared product.

(The membership of this enum is internal product naming and is not published on this site.)

ID Conventions

Artifact ID format Source of ID
Initiative I-YYYY-XX-NNN Directory path
Experiment E-YYYY-XX-NNN File name
PRD PRD-YYYY-XX-NNN File name / path
Implementation IMPL-YYYY-XX-NNN File name / path
Product Proposal PROP-YYYY-XX-NNN (^PROP-[0-9]{4}-[A-Z]{2,3}-[0-9]{3}$) Frontmatter id:
Decision DEC-YYYY-NNN (^DEC-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{3}$) Frontmatter id:
Team Charter TC-NNN File name teams/TC-NNN-{slug}.md
Pod Charter PC-NNN File name pods/PC-NNN-{slug}.md
Guild Charter GC-NNN File name guilds/GC-NNN-{slug}.md
Doc DOC-YYYY-NNN (^DOC-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{3,4}$, generated) Frontmatter id: (/apex-generate-docs)
Design / Proposal / Policy / Guide / Wiki / Update / RFC / PRD Review none Path-scoped (prd-review is scoped under its parent PRD)

XX is the 2–3 letter product/initiative code (e.g., GC, FOR, APX); YYYY is the year; NNN is a zero-padded sequence. Slugs are kebab-case and match the branch slug (see 04-workflow.md).

APEX Workflow & Governance {#SPEC-APEXSPEC-05~draft}

Status: Normative · Subsystem: APEXSPEC · Last-updated: 2026-06-01 · Spec ID: SPEC-APEXSPEC-05~draft

Status Lifecycles

Each artifact type has an exact status lifecycle. The diagrams below are normative; no transition outside them is valid. (Note: shipped and delivered are schema-valid initiative statuses but are unused in practice — use deployed. The initiative diagram below intentionally omits them, as no initiative on disk carries either value.)

Initiative

Code ordering: discovery(0) validated(1) delivery(2) deployed(3) learning(4) success(5) killed(6). killed is reachable from any state.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> discovery
    discovery --> validated
    validated --> delivery
    delivery --> deployed
    deployed --> learning
    learning --> success
    discovery --> killed
    validated --> killed
    delivery --> killed
    deployed --> killed
    learning --> killed
    success --> [*]
    killed --> [*]

Experiment

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> planned
    planned --> running
    running --> completed
    completed --> [*]

Outcome (on completion): validated | invalidated | inconclusive | null.

PRD

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft
    draft --> review
    review --> approved
    approved --> in_development
    in_development --> deployed
    deployed --> learning
    learning --> [*]

Implementation

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft
    draft --> review
    review --> approved
    approved --> in_progress
    in_progress --> complete
    complete --> [*]

Proposal (global)

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft
    draft --> review
    review --> approved
    approved --> implemented
    draft --> rejected
    review --> rejected
    implemented --> [*]
    rejected --> [*]

implemented and rejected are terminal ⇒ apex archive moves to archive/proposals/.

Product Proposal

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft
    draft --> approved
    approved --> in_progress
    in_progress --> delivered
    draft --> rejected
    draft --> duplicate
    draft --> parked
    delivered --> [*]
    rejected --> [*]
    duplicate --> [*]
    parked --> [*]

A proposal moves from approved to in_progress when an initiative is created to deliver this proposal. Entries in related_initiatives (topical adjacency to pre-existing initiatives) do not trigger the transition — only a new initiative created as the delivery vehicle for this proposal's idea does.

Decision

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> proposed
    proposed --> accepted
    accepted --> deprecated
    accepted --> superseded
    deprecated --> [*]
    superseded --> [*]

Once accepted, a decision is never edited — supersede with a new DEC instead.

Design

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> proposed
    proposed --> accepted
    accepted --> superseded
    superseded --> [*]

Policy / Guide / Wiki

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft
    draft --> approved
    approved --> obsolete
    approved --> migrated
    obsolete --> [*]
    migrated --> [*]

For policies, merge to main = approved. migrated is a schema-valid terminal status (schemas/frontmatter.schema.json — policy/guide/wiki status.enum) marking content relocated to another system (e.g. a Confluence-migrated wiki page); it is a sink like obsolete.

Update

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft
    draft --> published
    published --> [*]

RFC

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft
    draft --> open
    open --> accepted
    open --> rejected
    open --> withdrawn
    accepted --> [*]
    rejected --> [*]
    withdrawn --> [*]

Branch-Naming Prefixes

Branch prefix signals the artifact type or nature of the work. Slug matches the initiative directory or proposal filename.

Prefix When to use
initiative/ Creating or updating an Initiative.md
proposal/ A proposal awaiting review
experiment/ An experiment artifact
prd/ A PRD artifact
impl/ An implementation plan
guide/ A guide in guides/
policy/ A policy in policies/
decision/ A decision record
design/ A technical design within an initiative
team/ A team charter
pod/ A pod charter
guild/ A guild charter
fix/ Status updates, minor corrections
feature/ Multi-artifact changes (schema + skills + templates)
docs/ Framework docs only (not a new guide/policy artifact)
chore/ CI, tooling, repo maintenance
arb/ Architecture Review Board tooling and measurement work — schema fields, architecture rules, and ARB experiments under the architecture-review-tooling initiative
feat/ DEPRECATED — use feature/

PR Workflow & Pod-Merge Eligibility

Config: pod-merge-config.yml + .github/scripts/check-pod-merge.py.

Always-allowed approvers: two named leadership groups may merge any pull request regardless of initiative status. Their membership is configured in pod-merge-config.yml and is not published on this site.

Pod members (pm / tech_lead / designer / engineering_manager of a pod) may approve-to-merge only for their own pod's product path, and only when every affected initiative is in a delivery-eligible status, defined as:

{ delivery, deployed, learning, success }

That is: a pod member cannot merge a PR that touches an initiative still in discovery or validated — those require a PLT/SELT approver.

Eligibility algorithm (check-pod-merge.py)

  1. Collect the PR's approvers and changed files.
  2. If there are no approvals → pass (nothing to gate yet).
  3. If no products/ files changed → pass.
  4. If any approver is PLT or SELT → pass.
  5. Identify pod-member approvers (a member of any pod). If none → pass.
  6. For each changed products/{domain}/{product}/… path, walk up to the nearest Initiative.md and read its status. If there is none → pass for that path (a README or product-level file has no stage to gate).
  7. Resolve the pod that owns that product path in pod-merge-config.yml: exact match first, then the longest prefix on a path-segment boundary — so onboarding/setup uses its own entry, while the unlisted onboarding/newthing falls back to onboarding. A path with no entry, or one whose roles are all null (e.g. hotstats), resolves to an empty member set.
  8. If no approver belongs to that path's pod → BLOCK. Pod membership does not carry across paths: the onboarding PM is a non-pod approver for hotstats/… files, and an empty member set leaves PLT/SELT as the only way through.
  9. If that path's status ∉ {delivery, deployed, learning, success} → BLOCK.
  10. Otherwise → pass.

Note: a CI workflow invoking check-pod-merge.py was not found wired on main as of this writing — see DISC-5. The script and config exist; automated enforcement is the gap.

Reviewer auto-assignment

assign-reviewers.yml auto-requests the pod's pm and tech_lead as reviewers when a PR is opened (excluding the author).

Discovery → Delivery → Learning Pipeline

The /apex-* command chain that advances an initiative end to end:

/apex-initiative           # create initiative (status: discovery)
  → /apex-experiment (1+)   # run experiments
  → /apex-update-initiative # re-synthesize Initiative.md, bump version
  → /apex-transition            # status: validated
  → /apex-prd               # generate PRD
  → /apex-transition            # PRD status: approved
  → /apex-implementation    # engineering execution plan
  → /apex-epic              # PRD → JIRA epic
  → [engineering delivery]
  → /apex-ship              # status: deployed
  → /apex-measure           # metrics at T+7 / T+30
  → /apex-learn             # retrospective (status: learning → success)

Gates:

  • eng_exec_sponsor is schema-required before delivery (hard gate).
  • PRD review for high/critical risk is a soft gate (/apex-prd-review).
  • A new delivery initiative must have a PRD.md (convention). Confluence-migrated initiatives may be in delivery without a PRD — acknowledged debt; new ones must not.

Governance Layer

Mechanism Current state
Auto-merge-on-approve ENABLED.
Required checks validate-frontmatter, check-pod-merge.
PR stale-reaper (stale.yml) 14d no activity → stale label; +16d → close. Exempt labels: keep-open, do-not-merge. delete-branch: false (never deletes branches).
Weekly PR triage (pr-triage.yml) Weekly → maintains a "Weekly PR Triage" tracking issue.
Initiative staleness (stale-initiatives.yml) Mon 9am: initiatives in discovery/validated older than 30d → a Slack channel.
