APEX Validation & Tooling {#SPEC-APEXSPEC-06~draft}

Status: Normative · Subsystem: APEXSPEC · Last-updated: 2026-07-31 · Spec ID: SPEC-APEXSPEC-06~draft

Frontmatter Schema Mechanics

Source: schemas/frontmatter.schema.json.

  • Draft: JSON Schema Draft-07 ("$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#").
  • Discriminator: the type field is a const per branch of the root dispatch. The definitions block holds 24 entries: the 20 per-artifact-type definitions plus 4 shared subschemas (date, product_slug, tagList, schemaVersion).
  • Root dispatch (allOf + if/then, not oneOf): the top-level schema is a type-discriminated allOf chain of 20 if (type == const) then $ref branches — one per artifact type — not an undiscriminated oneOf. An unknown type therefore yields exactly ONE error (the value is not in the root type enum) instead of failing against all 20 branches at once. Validation semantics are otherwise unchanged: required: [type] preserves the missing-type failure and each if/then applies exactly one definition. See schemas/frontmatter.schema.json $comment-root-dispatch and the canonical-data-model effort (PR1); the full rationale is in 09-canonical-datamodel.md.
  • additionalProperties: true: unknown frontmatter fields are warnings, not errors. This permits forward-compatible fields but means typos are not hard failures.
  • allOf + if/then: conditional requireds are expressed as allOf clauses, e.g. an initiative with status: discovery additionally requires metric_target, hypothesis, author, pod; status ∈ {delivery, deployed, learning, success} additionally requires eng_exec_sponsor; a product-proposal with source: customer additionally requires customer_name.
  • schemaVersion: optional MAJOR.MINOR field (pattern ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$) on every artifact type, recording the schema contract the artifact was authored against. It is never required and defaults to absent; when present it is format-validated. It backs the deprecation runway (#791) — see Deprecation Runway below.

Deprecation Runway (#791)

When a validator rule tightens (deprecating a field, requiring a new one), every downstream author hits the new error at once, forcing batch-fix PRs that thrash the long tail of contributors. To avoid this, rule changes ship on a deprecation runway: a finding is a non-blocking DEPRECATION (warning) first, then is automatically promoted to a hard ERROR once the schema version reaches a declared promotion version.

  • Current schema version: the single source of truth is SCHEMA_VERSION in packages/apex-tools/src/apex/services/deprecations.py (currently 1.0). apex validate prints it in the ## Deprecations section of its report.
  • Registry: each deprecation is a registered Deprecation with a stable machine-readable code (e.g. DEP-001), the version it was deprecated_in, the version it is promoted to an error in (promote_in), the human-facing promote_on date, and a migration_url.
  • Runway gate: a deprecation is a warning while SCHEMA_VERSION < promote_in, and an error once SCHEMA_VERSION >= promote_in (numeric MAJOR.MINOR comparison).
  • ERROR vs DEPRECATION: ERRORs always block; DEPRECATIONs are advisory until their runway elapses. The validate-apex.yml merge gate (#788) respects this distinction.
  • Machine-readable output: every deprecation message carries a stable suffix [DEPRECATION DEP-NNN | becomes error in vX.Y on YYYY-MM-DD | <migration_url>] (the tag becomes DEPRECATION-PROMOTED once it is an error). This lets the warning auto-tracker (#793) dedup and open/close tracking issues by code.
  • Currently registered: DEP-001 (frontmatter id), DEP-002 (time_box/DISC-7), DEP-003 (repos.yaml initiative field). All are pinned to promote_in: 2.0 so existing files that still carry them remain warnings — the runway must never retroactively break files that predate the discipline.

The full author-facing lifecycle (how to deprecate a rule, runway length) is documented in docs/CONTRIBUTING.md.

Validation Passes

apex validate runs the passes below, in the order ValidationService.validate calls them (packages/apex-tools/src/apex/services/validation.py — the method list there is authoritative; an earlier revision of this section said "nine passes" while the code ran seventeen, which is exactly the count-drift failure DISC-10/DISC-13 record for skills):

  1. Unknown types — the single filesystem walk collects the artifact set and errors on unrecognised type: values.
  2. Schema + cross-references — validate frontmatter against the per-type schema branch; resolve related_experiments/related_prd, sponsor requirements, Experiment/PRD/ Implementation parent_initiative (spec 08-repo-linkage.md §2.2/§3 — dangling is an error; a field-less Implementation warns pending backfill), depends_on/ related_initiatives (+ cycle detection). Also resolves parent_prd on implementation/prd-review → a present value that does not resolve, or resolves to a non-prd artifact, WARNS (WARN-first runway, spec 08-repo-linkage.md §3/E2 — 3 real Implementations still name an initiative slug there).
  3. Duplicate artifact IDs — global uniqueness over the effective ID (explicit id: else path-derived).
  4. Deprecated fields — runway-classified findings: id: outside decision/product-proposal (DEP-001), time_box on initiatives/experiments (DEP-002). Warning until promote_in, then error. See Deprecation Runway.
  5. Architecture declaration — gate artifacts (implementation, design, rfc, decision) must carry an architecture block declaring the surface they touch across the ten Lane B triggers in policies/engineering/architecture-decision-policy.md. Severity is filter-aware, and deliberately so: an artifact in scope of --filter-paths that is missing the block is an ERROR, while an unfiltered run reports the artifacts that predate the requirement as a single aggregate WARNING. That split is the mechanism behind the requirement being non-retroactive — a pull request is validated against its changed files, so an author is blocked only on an artifact they are already editing, whereas the push-to-main run is unfiltered and would otherwise fail on every artifact written before the rule existed, which is the bulk backfill the policy rules out. The block's shape is owned by the schema (every trigger key required, an empty list being a positive claim rather than a blank); only its presence is owned by this pass. Unlike most new rules this one is fail-closed from the start rather than using the Deprecation Runway: the runway exists to spread the cost of touching files nobody planned to touch, and this rule only ever fires on a file someone is already editing.
  6. Directory placement — the artifact's path/bucket must match its type, domain, product, and status. The five long-standing types (initiative, experiment, prd, design, product-proposal) keep their bespoke rules; every other loaded in-scope type additionally gets a schema-driven, WARN-only IA-placement check that compares its on-disk path against the directory segments implied by its x-apex-path-template and (where present) matches the filename against its x-apex-id-pattern (team-charter, pod-charter, guild-charter, decision, implementation, policy, guide, wiki, update, rfc, prd-review, proposal). These findings are ADVISORY — they never add to errors nor flip result.passed. proposal and guild-charter are folded into this common SchemaModel-driven check; their bespoke ERROR passes (#9, #13) are unchanged and still own placement enforcement.
  7. repos.yaml — validate against schemas/repos.schema.json; emit DEP-003 for the deprecated initiative: key on both carriers — the top-level key and per-repository entries (#1403 closed the top-level blind spot).
  8. Binary files in products/ — size warnings >10 MB, errors >25 MB.
  9. Cross-reference link integrity — internal markdown links under products/ resolve.
  10. Proposal location — proposals live under proposals/; terminal ones under archive/proposals/.
  11. Proposal schema compliance — per-type status enums for proposal vs product-proposal.
  12. Gitignore violations — tracked files matching ignore patterns.
  13. Pod-charter match — every initiative pod: resolves to a pod-charter team_name.
  14. Guild charter — placement, GC-NNN- filename, status enum, elt_sponsor.
  15. Member allocation — per-person allocation across pod-charters (>100% error, <100% warning).
  16. Initiative pod required — non-terminal initiatives must carry pod:.
  17. Pod-merge-config coverage — config handles must appear in an active pod-charter.
  18. Update periods — period_end >= period_start on update artifacts.
  19. Docs skill count — documented Cursor-skill counts match .cursor/skills/.
  20. Linkage fields outside artifacts — parent_initiative in files the loader skips is parsed independently and must resolve to an initiative slug (WARNING; spec 08-repo-linkage.md §2.2(c), closed G12/DISC-19).
  21. NCM — ncm_ref: backlinks resolve (file + GitHub-slugged anchor) and **NCM:** implementer blocks in docs/spec/ have reciprocal backlinks (WARNING; closed G8).
  22. External-ID registry — docs/initiative-id-registry.yaml (the declaration site for I-YYYY-XX-NNN IDs) is internally sound: unique, well-formed IDs in registered namespaces, every active slug resolving to a real initiative, at most one active ID per initiative, retired rows keeping slug: null (ERRORS); deprecated legacy carriers (repos.yaml initiative:, frontmatter initiative_id:) reconcile against it (WARNINGS until DEP-003 deletes them). Spec 08-repo-linkage.md §10.2; closed G1/G2/G13.
  23. Supersession links — resolve every superseded_by reference on the six types that carry a superseded_by linkage edge (guild-charter, pod-charter, decision, design, policy, wiki). ID-bearing types (GC-NNN, PC-NNN, DEC-YYYY-NNN) are keyed by the canonical ID prefix extracted from path.stem via x-apex-id-pattern (their files are named {ID}-{slug}.md, so a naive stem lookup of a bare PC-020 would miss PC-020-DevOps-Charter); ID-less types (design, policy, wiki) resolve by full path.stem. A present reference that does not resolve — or resolves to the wrong target type — WARNS. Every covered type is loaded by the walk, decision included since docs/decisions/ became a scan root (G15). These findings are ADVISORY — WARN-first, never errors: referential enforcement rides a promote-to-ERROR runway (the same pattern parent_initiative/G3 rode). parent_prd resolution on implementation/prd-review (pass #2) is on the same runway.

Plus a CI step: scripts/validate_yaml_keys.py.

The apex CLI

Install: pip install -e packages/apex-tools/.

Multi-worktree hazard: pip install -e pins an editable install to the absolute source path of the worktree it was run from. This repo is routinely worked on via many concurrent git worktrees (.worktrees/*, .claude/worktrees/agent-*) — running apex from any worktree OTHER than the one you installed from silently loads that other worktree's code while operating on your current worktree's files. apex detects this case (same repository, different worktree top-level) and prints a loud warning naming both paths plus the exact remedy; a legitimate global/venv/pipx install never triggers it. If you see the warning, either run with the correct source on PYTHONPATH (PYTHONPATH=<this-worktree>/packages/apex-tools/src python3 -m apex.cli.main ...) or reinstall editable from the worktree you're actually in. Set APEX_STRICT_WORKTREE_GUARD=1 to make the mismatch a hard, nonzero-exit failure instead of a warning (e.g. in CI). See detect_worktree_mismatch in packages/apex-tools/src/apex/cli/main.py.

Root resolution: the CLI walks up from the cwd to the first directory containing both products/ and schemas/, or uses an explicit --root.

Command Purpose Flags
apex validate Run all validation passes --root, --schema, --repos-schema, --filter-paths
apex migrate Move initiatives to correct status buckets --root, --execute (dry-run by default)
apex status-change Transition an initiative's status (and move its directory) --initiative, --new-status, --execute
apex archive Move terminal proposals to archive/proposals/ --execute
apex check-links Validate markdown link integrity --fix, --exclude, --no-default-excludes

check-links default excludes: .claude, .claude-backup, .claude-mpm, .cursor, archive, plugins, templates, website/node_modules, website/build, website/.docusaurus.

Pre-Commit Hook

Install via bash scripts/hooks/install-hooks.sh (symlinks scripts/hooks/pre-commit into the repo's git hooks; works from the primary checkout or a linked worktree). The hook has two responsibilities, run in order:

  1. Auto-version-bump of changed initiatives (below).
  2. Validation enforcement — runs apex validate + apex check-links and blocks the commit on errors CI would otherwise flag (below).

Requires the apex CLI (pip install -e packages/apex-tools/). If apex is not on PATH, validation is skipped with a warning and CI remains the backstop.

Auto-Version-Bump

Behavior: when a staged Initiative.md has changed but its version was not already bumped in the commit, the hook auto-bumps the MINOR version (MAJOR.MINOR), appends a version_history entry ({version, date, change}), and re-stages the file. This guarantees every initiative content change carries a version increment.

Validation Enforcement

After the version bump, the hook validates the commit so authors catch frontmatter and link errors locally instead of failing CI (where they previously blocked open PRs):

  • apex validate --root . --filter-paths <staged files> — frontmatter/schema validation scoped to the staged artifacts, mirroring the --filter-paths behavior CI uses on PRs. Full-repo apex validate --root . is intentionally not used as the gate: main carries a few pre-existing repo-wide errors in unrelated artifacts, so a full-repo gate would block every commit. Scoping to staged files catches exactly what CI would flag on your PR.
  • apex check-links --root . with the same --exclude set as validate-apex.yml (.claude, .claude-mpm, .cursor, archive, plugins, templates, website).

On failure the commit is blocked (exit 1) with the offending errors and remediation guidance.

Emergency bypass: git commit --no-verify skips all hooks. Use sparingly — CI will still fail on the same errors.

version_history Entry Shape (DISC-8)

Each version_history entry is an object with exactly these three keys (additionalProperties: false — no extra keys permitted):

Key Type Meaning
version string The version this entry records (e.g. "1.3").
date date (YYYY-MM-DD) The date the change was made.
change string One-line description of what changed.

Example:

version_history:
  - version: "1.0"
    date: 2026-03-01
    change: "Initiative created"
  - version: "1.1"
    date: 2026-04-12
    change: "Advanced to delivery; added eng_exec_sponsor"

The pre-commit hook (scripts/hooks/pre-commit) auto-appends a new entry in this exact shape whenever it bumps an initiative's version. Authors may also append entries manually, but must match the shape — any extra key is a schema error.

CI Workflows

Workflow Trigger Purpose
validate-apex.yml PR + push to main Forbidden-files check, validate_yaml_keys.py, check-links, apex validate (--filter-paths on PR, full on push), a second check-links, and a PR comment with the result.
stale-initiatives.yml Mon 9am discovery/validated initiatives older than 30d → a Slack channel.
assign-reviewers.yml PR open Auto-request the pod's pm + tech_lead (excluding author).
label-pr.yml PR Labels by changed paths (type:initiative/prd/policy/guide/team/proposal/design/ci/tooling); falls back to branch prefix.
stale.yml scheduled PR stale-reaper: 14d → stale; +16d → close; delete-branch: false.
pr-triage.yml weekly Maintains the "Weekly PR Triage" tracking issue.
tier-classifier.yml PR open/sync/reopen Runs apex classify-pr, comments the per-file tier table, applies a tier:* label, and squash-merges auto-merge-eligible Tier 0 PRs via the dedicated apex-companion App (the sole bypass actor — DEC-2026-009).

PR tier classification

apex classify-pr (packages/apex-tools/src/apex/services/pr_classifier.py) assigns each changed file a tier and the PR inherits the highest tier of any file it touches:

Tier What lands here Review
0 Meeting notes, discovery/planning material, tickets, release-notes, assets, and Update artifacts None — bot-gated auto-merge
1 Existing core artifact with administrative-only frontmatter changes; any other file inside products/ 1 CODEOWNERS approval
2 New core artifacts, substantive changes, anything ambiguous or unreadable Full CODEOWNERS review

Two rules bound what Tier 0 can admit:

  • Update artifacts must satisfy path and frontmatter. A file qualifies only when its path matches products/…/initiatives/{slug}/updates/YYYY-MM-DD-{slug}.md and its own frontmatter declares type: update. A markdown file merely sitting in an updates/ directory does not qualify, and a deleted, renamed, retyped, or unreadable file never reaches Tier 0.
  • Retyping blocks auto-merge. If any changed file's frontmatter type value differs between the base ref and the PR, the PR is not auto-merge eligible regardless of tier — an artifact cannot be relabelled into a Tier 0 shape to skip review.

Product docs/ files are deliberately not Tier 0 (they routinely hold tech specs — see PR #835, the cautionary case in DEC-2026-009). Anything the classifier cannot read or classify fails closed to Tier 2; an empty in-scope set is Tier 2, never Tier 0.

MCP Server

packages/apex-mcp — the local, stdio-transport, unauthenticated MCP server previously documented here (23 tools, configured via APEX_ROOT) — was retired and removed per DEC-2026-018. The canonical APEX MCP surface is now APEX Companion's hosted MCP server (apex_companion/mcp/, OAuth 2.1 PKCE, 30+ tools) at the APEX Companion app — note this connector endpoint is a different host than the Companion web app (the APEX Companion app).

Note (DISC-6 resolved, then closed-by-retirement — see 07-known-discrepancies.md): the initiative subtypes customer_facing and internal_engineering and their extra fields (project_type, asset_types, service_classes, personas, engineering_category, customer_requested, customer_name, new_data_source, data_source_description, and deal_impact) were canonicalized into definitions.initiative in schemas/frontmatter.schema.json (with enum constraints) while apex-mcp still existed. That schema canonicalization is unaffected by the package's removal — these remain first-class, validated frontmatter properties regardless of which MCP surface writes them.

title: Skills & Agents
blurb: The full skills catalog grouped by category, plus the agent roster.
html:
APEX Skills & Agents {#SPEC-APEXSPEC-07~draft}

Status: Normative · Subsystem: APEXSPEC · Last-updated: 2026-07-15 · Spec ID: SPEC-APEXSPEC-07~draft

Cursor Skills Catalog (41)

Location: .cursor/skills/. Each skill is a directory containing a SKILL.md. Invoked as /apex-* slash commands, except duetto-apex-maintenance, which is invoked as /duetto-apex-maintenance, and apex-artifacts, which is auto-activated reference knowledge rather than a command. Every skill in this catalog exists in both the .cursor/skills/ and .claude/skills/ trees — see "Skill Deployment Locations" below. Grouped by workflow category:

Setup

Skill Purpose
apex-help Show all available APEX commands and their purposes.
apex-setup Configure git identity and verify GitHub access.
apex-git-setup Set up recommended local git config (fetch.prune, git gone alias) and a Cursor session hook that auto-syncs main and cleans up merged branches.

Proposals

Skill Purpose
apex-proposal Create/update a proposal — global (type: proposal) or product-level (type: product-proposal).
apex-vote Upvote or downvote a product proposal to signal demand.
apex-wiki Create or update a wiki article in wiki/{domain}/.

Discovery

Skill Purpose
apex-initiative Create a new initiative directory (includes the Context Gathering Protocol).
apex-experiment Create an experiment or record its outcome within an initiative.

Specification

Skill Purpose
apex-prd Generate a PRD from initiative context.
apex-prd-review Score PRD implementability across 5 dimensions; gate before approved.

Planning

Skill Purpose
apex-tests Generate a Test Manifest from an approved PRD.
apex-implementation Create an engineering execution plan linked to an approved PRD.
apex-epic Convert an approved PRD to a JIRA epic with user stories.

Delivery

Skill Purpose
apex-ship Record a deployment milestone; transition the initiative to deployed.

Learning

Skill Purpose
apex-measure Record a metrics checkpoint (T+7 / T+30) to evaluate success.
apex-learn Document learnings and create a retrospective.

Documentation & Comms

Skill Purpose
apex-generate-docs Generate a doc artifact (DOC-YYYY-NNN) for a shipped/delivered initiative from its three-pillar context (Apex artifacts, repo docs, JIRA tickets); PM-triggered, PM-reviewed, never bot-committed. Status: Phase-1 stub — full generation lands with PROP-2026-DOC-001 Phase 2.
apex-newsletter Create an individual, dated newsletter update under newsletters/{product|engineering}/updates/YYYY-MM-DD-{slug}.md for the apex-companion "What's New" hub. Does not create edition-level roll-ups (editions/) — those are handled by the create_newsletter_edition MCP tool and curation.
apex-newsletter-edition Orchestrate the list_newsletter_editions / get_newsletter_edition / create_newsletter_edition / publish_newsletter_edition MCP tools plus a narrative-synthesis curation pass to draft, curate, and publish a monthly newsletters/{product|engineering}/editions/ roll-up. Never hand-writes edition files; defers to newsletters/{domain}/README.md for schema.

Records

Skill Purpose
apex-decision Create an ADR-style decision record.
apex-policy Create or update a standing operating policy.
apex-guide Create or update a step-by-step guide.
apex-charter Create or update a team charter.

Reference

Skill Purpose
apex-artifacts Artifact quick reference — the per-type frontmatter tables are generated from schemas/frontmatter.schema.json, plus the rules the schema cannot state (object-vs-string gotchas, cross-reference semantics, status transitions, tag conventions). Auto-activated contextual knowledge; not a slash command.

Status & Workflow

Skill Purpose
apex-status Display the status of all initiatives and pipeline position.
apex-dashboard Generate a cross-product pipeline status dashboard.
apex-report Generate a comprehensive product/team status report (saved locally).
apex-transition Transition any artifact's status field, validating the transition is legal.
apex-update-initiative Re-synthesize Initiative.md from subdirectory context and bump version.
apex-validate Validate frontmatter and document links.
apex-commit Create a conventional commit with proper formatting.
apex-session-sync Capture session learnings as APEX artifacts — insights, decisions, and occasionally formal experiments — classified and written to the right places. Also auto-activates at end of session or on "sync to APEX" / "push learnings".
apex-meeting-prep Initiative health check and bi-weekly meeting-prep report. Reads the Initiative → Experiments → PRDs → Implementation → JIRA tree, computes per-dimension health signals, and emits a "Needed Next" action per initiative. Also answers to /apex-initiative-health for the single-initiative case.
duetto-apex-maintenance Autonomous routine repo maintenance scoped to a single codeowner's owner-space — any codeowner runs this to triage, auto-fix, and report on only the PRs, issues, and artifacts they own. Invoked as /duetto-apex-maintenance, not /apex-*.

PR

Skill Purpose
apex-pr-create Create a pull request with APEX conventions.
apex-pr-report Personalized PR review report — what needs your attention.
apex-pr-review Review a PR systematically with structured checklists.
apex-pr-approve Approve a pull request with an optional comment.
apex-pr-comment Add a comment to a pull request.
apex-pr-request-changes Request changes with structured feedback.

Deprecated

Skill Purpose
apex-meeting Deprecated — drop meeting transcripts directly into meetings/ instead.

Total: 41 skills.

Claude Code Agents (7)

Location: .claude/agents/.

Agent Role
research Investigation, codebase/context gathering, deep research.
engineer Implementation and code changes.
qa Test execution and quality verification.
ops Operations, CI/CD, infrastructure tasks.
documentation Documentation authoring and reorganization.
ticketing JIRA / issue management.
web-qa Browser-driven web application testing.

Skill Deployment Locations

APEX maintains three skill trees with different formats and purposes:

1. .cursor/skills/ (Canonical Command Skills — 41 skills)

Location: .cursor/skills/ Format: Each skill is a directory containing SKILL.md with a # APEX {Name} heading. Scope: Complete procedure definitions for all APEX workflows. Invocation: Cursor IDE slash commands (/apex-*). Tracking: Fully committed to git (not gitignored).

The .cursor/skills/ tree is the authoritative source for skill procedure, content, and validation. Every command skill documented in the catalog above lives here.

2. .claude/skills/ (Claude Code Deployments — 41 skills)

Location: .claude/skills/ Tracking: Gitignored by default; the apex-* and duetto-apex-maintenance entries are re-included by name (see 2c). Scope: Every skill in the catalog above appears here. Two forms:

2a. Stubs (5-line mirror files)

Every command skill in this directory is a 5-line stub that reads .cursor/skills/ for the full procedure:

# /apex-name

Short description of what this does.

Read `.cursor/skills/apex-name/SKILL.md` and execute it exactly as written. Forward any arguments the user provided as the first input to the interactive flow.

A stub may carry YAML frontmatter (name, description, when_to_use, …) ahead of the heading when Claude Code needs it to auto-activate the skill — apex-session-sync and apex-meeting-prep do. That metadata belongs on the Claude side; the procedure stays in .cursor/skills/, which remains authoritative (precedence layer 3).

2b. Generated Full-Content Reference (apex-artifacts)

apex-artifacts is the one skill that is full content in both trees rather than canonical-plus-stub. It is auto-activated reference knowledge, so the content must be in context on both platforms without a file-read hop, and the generator — not a stub pointer — is what keeps the copies identical. See "Code Generation" below.

Before #2039 this section listed apex-session-sync and apex-artifacts as skills that existed ONLY in .claude/skills/ and could not be used from Cursor. That exception is retired: all skills now support both platforms.

2c. Gitignore Behavior

.gitignore ignores .claude/skills/* (a file glob, deliberately not a directory-level .claude/skills/ rule, which would stop git descending and break the negations below), then re-includes by name:

  • !.claude/skills/apex-*/ and !.claude/skills/apex-*/** — every apex-* skill, so a newly mirrored one is tracked with no further gitignore edit
  • !.claude/skills/duetto-apex-maintenance/ and !.claude/skills/duetto-apex-maintenance/**
  • !.claude/skills/mpm-message/ and !.claude/skills/mpm-message/** — a project-customized non-APEX skill

Why? The apex-* skills are project-customized and part of the canonical repository. Most user-installed Claude skills are per-contributor machine state, so they are gitignored; APEX skills are the exception.

3. plugins/skills/ (Contextual Knowledge Plugins — 3 skills)

Location: plugins/skills/ Format: Each skill is a directory with a SKILL.md containing YAML frontmatter with name and description fields. Includes real YAML frontmatter (not markdown stubs):

---
name: apex-governance
description: APEX status transition rules and validation requirements for artifact lifecycle management.
---

Scope: Auto-triggered contextual knowledge (not user-invoked commands):

  • apex-governance — Status transition rules and validation requirements
  • apex-workflow — Workflow integration and best practices
  • apex-artifacts — Artifact structure and field reference (auto-triggered alongside the command skill)

These plugins provide semantic context to the AI without requiring a slash command — they activate based on user intent and conversation context.

Note: apex-artifacts appears in all three trees — .cursor/skills/ and .claude/skills/ as the reference skill, plugins/skills/ as a contextual knowledge plugin. All three copies are generated.

Code Generation

Only apex-artifacts is auto-generated:

  • Generator: packages/apex-tools/src/apex/services/artifact_reference.py
  • Sentinel markers: <!-- BEGIN GENERATED: apex-artifacts schema reference — do not edit by hand --> / <!-- END GENERATED: apex-artifacts schema reference -->
  • Target files: .cursor/skills/apex-artifacts/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/apex-artifacts/SKILL.md, and plugins/skills/apex-artifacts/SKILL.md, all rewritten by scripts/generate_artifact_reference.py
  • Drift test: packages/apex-tools/tests/test_artifact_reference_drift.py — regenerates and diffs to ensure every target matches the schema. Its _APEX_ARTIFACTS_TARGETS must stay in lockstep with the script's TARGETS.
  • Why: The schema-derived reference (ID patterns, required fields, status enums, etc.) was previously hand-maintained in two places and drifted. Generation ensures a single source of truth in schemas/frontmatter.schema.json.

All other skills are single-sourced in .cursor/skills/ and reached from .claude/skills/ through a stub pointer, so there is nothing to diff — the skill-count validation at validation.py:2287 compares counts only, not content.

Adding a New Command Skill

  1. Author in .cursor/skills/ — create apex-name/SKILL.md with full procedure and # APEX {Name} heading.
  2. Add 5-line stub in .claude/skills/ — create apex-name/SKILL.md that reads and delegates to the Cursor version. Add YAML frontmatter only if Claude Code needs it to auto-activate the skill.
  3. Commit both — the !.claude/skills/apex-*/ exception in .gitignore ensures the stub is tracked; no new gitignore entry is needed for an apex-* name.
  4. Add a catalog row — in this file and in .cursor/skills/README.md.
  5. Validate — run apex validate --root . to confirm the skill count reflects the new skill, and update the counts in this file and CLAUDE.md.

Precedence for Procedure

When a skill exists in both trees:

  1. Layer 1: Claude Code /apex-* slash command user interface (most specific context)
  2. Layer 2: The .claude/skills/ implementation (stub or full content)
  3. Layer 3: The .cursor/skills/ SKILL.md definition (canonical procedure — all details go here)

title: Branch Naming Convention
blurb: Which branch prefix signals which kind of change.
html:
Branch Naming Convention

Overview

Branch names use a document-type prefix that matches the type of APEX artifact being created or modified. This makes the branch's purpose immediately clear from its name.

Workflow (#792): The Verify PR Artifact Type workflow cross-validates the branch prefix against the artifact-type checkbox in .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md and the paths of changed files, and posts an advisory comment on the PR. It does not block merge (ambiguous / multi-artifact PRs only warn), but use a prefix that accurately reflects the work to keep the signal clean. The feature/ prefix is the multi-artifact escape hatch and is exempt from the prefix-vs-type cross-check.

Pattern

{document-type}/{slug}

Prefixes

Artifact-Type Prefixes

Use when the primary purpose is creating or updating a specific APEX artifact. Prefix must match the artifact type.

Prefix Artifact Example
initiative/ Initiative.md initiative/ai-assistant
proposal/ Proposal document proposal/rest-forward-api-architecture
experiment/ Experiment experiment/rate-floor-ab-test
prd/ PRD prd/blockbuster-group-quote-v2
impl/ Implementation plan (IMPL-YYYY-XX-NNN) impl/booking-days-day-filter
guide/ Guide in guides/ guide/link-commits-to-tickets
policy/ Policy in policies/ policy/ai-tool-usage
decision/ Decision record (DEC-YYYY-NNN) decision/graphql-federation-rest-forward
design/ Technical architecture design within an initiative design/hotstats-self-serve-architecture
team/ Team Charter (TC-NNN) team/detection-charter
pod/ Pod Charter (PC-NNN) pod/blockbuster-charter
guild/ Guild Charter (GC-NNN) in guilds/ guild/quality-guild

Operational Prefixes

Use when the change spans multiple artifact types or doesn't create a new artifact.

Prefix When to use Example
fix/ Status updates, minor corrections, bug fixes fix/rooms-transient-mark-deployed
feature/ Multi-artifact changes (e.g. schema + skills + template together) feature/apex-apex-framework-initiative-linking
docs/ Changes to APEX framework docs only (not a new guide/policy artifact) docs/branch-naming-update
chore/ CI, tooling, repo maintenance chore/update-pre-commit-hooks
arb/ Architecture Review Board tooling and measurement work — schema fields, architecture rules, and ARB experiments under the architecture-review-tooling initiative arb/waiver-and-schema-fields-1976-1986

Examples

Good Branch Names

What you're doing Branch name
New initiative for AI assistant initiative/ai-assistant
New proposal for REST-forward API proposal/rest-forward-api-architecture
New engineer guide for ticket linking guide/link-commits-to-tickets
New AI tool usage policy policy/ai-tool-usage
New experiment for rate floor experiment/rate-floor-ab-test
New decision record decision/graphql-federation-rest-forward
Mark an initiative as deployed fix/rooms-transient-mark-deployed
Add a PRD to an initiative fix/ml-pricing-add-prd
Schema + skills + template change together feature/apex-apex-framework-initiative-linking
Update APEX docs only docs/branch-naming-update

Bad Branch Names

Branch Issue
feat/cloud-dev-sleds feat/ is not a recognized APEX prefix
docs/link-commits-to-tickets Wrong prefix for a guide artifact — use guide/
docs/ai-tool-usage Wrong prefix for a policy artifact — use policy/
feature/engineering-platform-infrastructure-cloud-dev-sleds Old domain-path pattern — don't embed the path
cloud-dev-sleds No type prefix
update-initiative Too vague, no slug

Slug Format

The {slug} should match the initiative directory name (or proposal filename without .md):

# Initiative at:
products/{domain}/{product}/

# Branch:
initiative/cloud-dev-sleds

# Proposal at:
proposals/APEX-MCP-SERVICE-PROPOSAL.md

# Branch:
proposal/apex-mcp-service

Quick Reference

# New initiative
git checkout -b initiative/{slug}

# New proposal
git checkout -b proposal/{slug}

# New guide
git checkout -b guide/{slug}

# New policy
git checkout -b policy/{slug}

# New experiment
git checkout -b experiment/{slug}

# New PRD
git checkout -b prd/{slug}

# New implementation plan

git checkout -b decision/{slug}

# New technical architecture design (scoped to an initiative)
git checkout -b design/{slug}

# Status update / fix
git checkout -b fix/{slug}-{action}
# e.g., fix/ml-pricing-mark-deployed

# Multi-artifact feature (schema + skills + templates etc.)
git checkout -b feature/{description}

# APEX framework docs only
git checkout -b docs/{description}
